RuleName: ADCS-001 - Cert Authority archived a key
Description: The rule detects if key is archived. This event is monitored to detect anomalous and malicious activity, and to prevent privilege abuse. Verify that approvment is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-002 - Cert Authority audit filter changed
Description: The rule identifies if the audit filter for Certificate Services changed. May indicate an attacker disabling monitoring in an attempt to cover their tracks prior to certificate activities.

RuleName: ADCS-003 - Certificate imported into database
Description: The rule detects if certificate imported into its database The imported certificate attributes should be verified. Also verify the legitimacy of this operation.

RuleName: ADCS-004 - Certificate manager settings changed
Description: The rule identifies if the certificate manager for Certificate Services changed. This action may indicate tampering with permissions with make users able to enroll on behalf of other users, commonly used to issue smart card certificates.

RuleName: ADCS-005 - Certificate request attribute changed
Description: The rule detects if certificate request attributes changed This event is monitored for anomalies and malicious activities, and for the possibility of restricted users and computers changing the attributes of a certificate request. This event should also be monitored for privilege abuse actions as well. Verify that approvment is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-006 - Certificate request extension change
Description: The rule detects if a certificate request extension changed. Changes in this category of object access events need to be monitored for possible privilege abuse and malicious activities. Verify that approvment is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-007 - CRL not been published
Description: The rule identifies if the CRL is published in the defined time period (threshold). Certificate revocation list (or CRL) is a list of digital certificates that have been revoked by the issuing CA before their scheduled expiration date and should no longer be trusted. A CRL is generated and published periodically, often at a defined interval. A missing CRL can impact the trustworthiness of certificates. We recommend checking the CRL status as soon as possible.

RuleName: ADCS-008 - Cert Authority configuration changed
Description: The rule detects when a configuration entry as Policy/Exit modules or CDP/AIA extensions changed in Certificate Services. This event is monitored to detect anomalous and malicious activity, and to prevent privilege abuse. Please investigate the legitimacy of the operation.

RuleName: ADCS-009 - Cert Authority Restarted or Stopped
Description: The rule monitors the Start and Stop operations of Active Directory Certificate Services. The consequences of stopping or restarting the CA service can have a direct impact on the environment. Please investigate the legitimacy of the operation.

RuleName: ADCS-010 - Cert Authority imported and archived a key
Description: The rule detects if key is imported and archived. This event is monitored to detect anomalous and malicious activity, and to prevent privilege abuse. Verify that approvment is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-011 - Cert Manager approves certificate request
Description: The rule detects if the Certificate manager approves pending certificate request. Issuance of certificates which require manual approval or certificates that contain usages that allow the owner to perform privileged operations (Enrollment Agent, Code Signing etc.) or certificates issued to VIP users should be monitored. Verify that approvment is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-012 - Cert Manager denied certificate request
Description: The rule detects if certificate request is denied by certificate manager. This event should be monitored to detect anomalous and malicious activity, and to prevent privilege abuse.

RuleName: ADCS-013 - CA certificate published to AD
Description: The rule detects when Certificate services published the CA certificate to Active Directory Domain services. This event is monitored to detect anomalous and malicious activity, and to prevent privilege abuse. Please investigate the legitimacy of the operation.

RuleName: ADCS-014 - Cert Authority registry value modified
Description: The rule detects if registry value of certification authority was modified. Any changes in CA registries should occur very rare. Please check the changes thoroughly.

RuleName: ADCS-015 - Cert Authority regular backup not completed
Description: The rule monitors regular backups of Active Directory Certificate Services. The regular backup should be completed If the backup was not completed in the required time, an incident is generated.

RuleName: ADCS-016 - Cert Authority retrieved an archived key
Description: The rule detects when Certificate services retrieved an archived key. This event is monitored to detect anomalous and malicious activity, and to prevent privilege abuse. Please investigate the legitimacy of the operation.

RuleName: ADCS-017 - Certificate Revoked
Description: The rule monitors if the certificate is revoked in Certificate Services. We recommend performing a verification if there are a large number of revocations. The incident will be generated if 2 (threshold) or more certificates are revoked.

RuleName: ADCS-018 - Cert Authority role separation state changed
Description: The rule detects if the ADCS Role separation state changed from changes from the expected value. (Set you expected status for each CA). If role separation status changed verify that this is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-019 - Rows deleted from Certification the database
Description: The rule detects if one or more rows has been deleted from the certificate database. Deleting rows may indicate an attacker covering their tracks after issuing certificates. Verify that this is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-020 - Security permissions changed on Certh Authority
Description: The rule monitors if the security permissions for Certificate Services changed. Changes may indicate an attacker granting permissions for other accounts to enroll. Verify that this is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-021 - Security of certificate template updated
Description: The rule monitors if the ADCS template security was updated. Changes may indicate an attacker granting permissions for other accounts to enroll certificate or modify templates. Verify that this is a valid operation.

RuleName: ADCS-022 - Unapproved certificate template loaded
Description: This rule evaluates loaded templates of Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) to the Certification Authority (CA). The rule monitors Event ID 4898 - Certificate Services loaded a template and correlates data from the watchlist 'CertAuthorities'. If it is determined that the parameters of the loaded template (TemplateInternalName, TemplateOID, pKIExtendedKeyUsage, or CaHostName) do not match the approved template, an alert is generated. The alert records: - Date and Time - isApprovedCaHostName, isApprovedCerTemplateName, isApprovedCertTemplateOID, isApprovedpKIExtendedKeyUsage, - CaName, CaHostName - Informations about loaded vs approved template Overall, this rule allows Security team to monitor and control the use of certificates using approved templates, which helps improve security and certificate management in the organization.

RuleName: ADCS-023 - Missing Certification Authority Heartbeat
Description: This detection will go over the heartbeats received from the agents of Certification Authorities over the last hour, and will create alerts if the last heartbeats were received an hour ago.

RuleName: ADCS-024 - Successful logon to Certification Authority server
Description: This query detects sucessfull remote or local logon to Certification Authority server. Connecting directly to a certification authority server should be very rare. All administration should be done through terminal servers or administration tools. Please verify the reason for the event

RuleName: AD FS Remote Auth Sync Connection
Description: This detection uses Security events from the "AD FS Auditing" provider to detect suspicious authentication events on an AD FS server. The results then get correlated with events from the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) to detect suspicious incoming network traffic on port 80 on the AD FS server. This could be a sign of a threat actor trying to use replication services on the AD FS server to get its configuration settings and extract sensitive information such as AD FS certificates. In order to use this query you need to enable AD FS auditing on the AD FS Server. References: https://docs.microsoft.com/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/troubleshooting/ad-fs-tshoot-logging https://twitter.com/OTR_Community/status/1387038995016732672

RuleName: ADFS DKM Master Key Export
Description: Identifies an export of the ADFS DKM Master Key from Active Directory. References: https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2020/12/13/customers-protect-nation-state-cyberattacks/, https://www.fireeye.com/blog/threat-research/2020/12/evasive-attacker-leverages-solarwinds-supply-chain-compromises-with-sunburst-backdoor.html?1 To understand further the details behind this detection, please review the details in the original PR and subequent PR update to this: https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/pull/1562#issue-551542469 https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/pull/1512#issue-543053339

RuleName: Azure Active Directory Hybrid Health AD FS New Server
Description: This detection uses AzureActivity logs (Administrative category) to identify the creation or update of a server instance in an Azure AD Hybrid Health AD FS service. A threat actor can create a new AD Health ADFS service and create a fake server instance to spoof AD FS signing logs. There is no need to compromise an on-premises AD FS server. This can be done programmatically via HTTP requests to Azure. More information in this blog: https://o365blog.com/post/hybridhealthagent/

RuleName: Azure Active Directory Hybrid Health AD FS Service Delete
Description: This detection uses AzureActivity logs (Administrative category) to identify the deletion of an Azure AD Hybrid Health AD FS service instance in a tenant. A threat actor can create a new AD Health ADFS service and create a fake server to spoof AD FS signing logs. The health AD FS service can then be deleted after it is no longer needed via HTTP requests to Azure. More information is available in this blog https://o365blog.com/post/hybridhealthagent/

RuleName: Azure Active Directory Hybrid Health AD FS Suspicious Application
Description: This detection uses AzureActivity logs (Administrative category) to identify a suspicious application adding a server instance to an Azure AD Hybrid Health AD FS service or deleting the AD FS service instance. Usually the Azure AD Connect Health Agent application with ID cf6d7e68-f018-4e0a-a7b3-126e053fb88d and ID cb1056e2-e479-49de-ae31-7812af012ed8 is used to perform those operations.

RuleName: Gain Code Execution on ADFS Server via Remote WMI Execution
Description: This query detects instances where an attacker has gained the ability to execute code on an ADFS Server through remote WMI Execution. In order to use this query you need to be collecting Sysmon EventIDs 19, 20, and 21. If you do not have Sysmon data in your workspace this query will raise an error stating: Failed to resolve scalar expression named "[@Name]" For more on how WMI was used in Solorigate see https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2021/01/20/deep-dive-into-the-solorigate-second-stage-activation-from-sunburst-to-teardrop-and-raindrop/. The query contains some features from the following detections to look for potentially malicious ADFS activity. See them for more details. - ADFS Key Export (Sysmon): https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/blob/master/Detections/SecurityEvent/ADFSKeyExportSysmon.yaml - ADFS DKM Master Key Export: https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/blob/master/Detections/MultipleDataSources/ADFS-DKM-MasterKey-Export.yaml

RuleName: Gain Code Execution on ADFS Server via SMB + Remote Service or Scheduled Task
Description: This query detects instances where an attacker has gained the ability to execute code on an ADFS Server through SMB and Remote Service or Scheduled Task.

RuleName: Active Domain Computers with Outdated Windows OS
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AD_Computers_CL table to identify enabled (active) Windows workstations that are not running the latest versions of the operating system. The rule excludes recently created, re-enabled, or deleted computers and focuses only on devices with the "Enabled" flag set to True. Outdated operating systems on active endpoints pose a significant risk, as they may lack security patches and be susceptible to known vulnerabilities. Attackers frequently exploit such systems for initial access, lateral movement, or persistence. Ensuring that active devices are up to date is vital for reducing attack surface and maintaining compliance with organizational security policies. Alert records: - Domain: The Active Directory domain of the computer. - Computer Name: Hostname of the active endpoint. - Canonical Name: Fully qualified domain name (FQDN). - Operating System: OS name and version (e.g., Windows 11 - 26100). - Object OU: Organizational Unit in AD where the object resides. - Created / Last Logon Date: Timestamps to understand the computer's lifecycle. Identifying outdated but active workstations is crucial for ensuring that production devices are secure, fully supported, and not exposing the organization to preventable threats.
Req. modification: latest version Win OS. SecurityEvent 4722,4741,4743 needed.

RuleName: Active Directory Object do NOT require password
Description: The rule checks for Computer and User object which have in “userAccountControll” attribute set to value “PASSWD_NOTREQD”. This represents a high security risk as the account is not protected at all without a password. To fix this issue change the value in the attribute. Default UAC values of objects are: User - 512 for enabled, 514 for disabled account. Computer - 4096 for enabled, 4098 for disabled account. More information about “userAccountControll” you can find on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/identity/useraccountcontrol-manipulate-account-properties

RuleName: BitLocker Recovery Key for object computer is missing in AD
Description: The rule detect if BitLocker Recovery Key for computer objects with Windows OS is missing in Active Directory. Computers created less than 3 days (threshold) are excluded from result for reducing false positive alerts for newly created computers. Active BitLocker and saved keys in Active Directory are important because they ensure encryption of data on computer disk drives. If these elements are turned off or missing, it can mean that data is at risk of leakage and unauthorized access, which can lead to a serious security incident.

RuleName: High value of inactive computer or user objects in AD
Description: The rule detects high value (threshold is set to 10%) of inactive computer or user objects in Active Directory. Inactivity is an imaginary object that has not logged in for more than 180 days (threshold). Inactive objects often stay in the network because of weaknesses in the decommissioning process. These stale computer or user accounts can be used as backdoors and therefore represents a possible security breach. To mitigate the risk, you should monitor the number of inactive accounts and reduce it as much as possible. A list of all inactive accounts is visible on Inactivity sheet of “Active Directory reports” workbook or directly via LogAnalytics.

RuleName: ADHC-001 - Outdated KRBTGT Password in Active Directory
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AD_Users_CL table collected via the AD Healthcheck (AMA) connector to identify KRBTGT accounts whose password has not been changed within the recommended period. The rule monitors the built-in KRBTGT account in Active Directory and detects when the PasswordLastSet value exceeds the defined threshold. An outdated KRBTGT password indicates insufficient Kerberos hygiene and increases security risk. The KRBTGT account is used to sign Kerberos Ticket Granting Tickets (TGTs). If compromised, attackers can forge Kerberos tickets (e.g., Golden Tickets) to maintain persistent and stealthy access. Regular password rotation is therefore critical to limit potential abuse. Alert records: - The Active Directory domain where the KRBTGT account was identified - KRBTGT account details - The timestamp of the last password change - The number of days since the password was last changed Monitoring this activity is essential because the KRBTGT account is central to Kerberos security. Regular password rotation reduces the risk of ticket forgery and helps limit attacker persistence in the environment.
Req. modification: krbtgt SID for custom accounts PWD last set threshold (180d recommended).

RuleName: AADR-001 - Access credential added to Microsoft Entra ID Application
Description: The rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID audit logs and detects when someone adds a new credential to an Application or Service Principal. If an attacker gains access to an account with sufficient privileges and adds alternate authentication material, they can authenticate as the Application or Service Principal using this credential. The alert records relevant and available details for analysis: - Application name, Object ID, and Client ID - Credential (Key) Information - Initiator, Initiator ID, and Initiator IP Address The rule allows us to promptly detect, analyze, investigate, and respond to unauthorized changes, helping to prevent unauthorized access and potential security breaches. In summary, monitoring the addition of new credentials enhances our security posture by providing early detection and mitigation of potential security risks.

RuleName: AADR-002 - Access from onion (TOR) network
Description: The rule detects access by a threat actor using the TOR network, which involves monitoring for connections to known TOR exit nodes. When a connection to a TOR exit node is detected, it triggers an alert that identifies: - the source IP address - User Account - Application - Sign-in status TOR exit nodes enable users to obscure their true IP address, making it challenging to trace or identify their actions. This anonymity is often exploited by cybercriminals for malicious activities, such as hacking, data theft, and other attacks. Unrestricted access from TOR exit nodes increases the risk of unauthorized access and brute force attacks. Additionally, TOR allows attackers to bypass geolocation restrictions and access systems meant for trusted networks. Frequent IP changes and encrypted traffic further complicate detection and blocking, making it difficult to identify or prevent potential threats effectively. This rule helps prevent malicious activity from being carried out using the anonymity provided by the TOR network.

RuleName: AADR-003 - Account Created and Deleted in Short Timeframe
Description: Search for user principal name (UPN) events. Look for accounts created and then deleted in under 24 hours. Attackers may create an account for their use, and then remove the account when no longer needed. Ref : https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/security-operations-user-accounts#short-lived-account

RuleName: AADR-004 - Addition of a Temporary Access Pass to a Privileged Account
Description: Detects when a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) is created for a Privileged Account. A Temporary Access Pass is a time-limited passcode issued by an admin that satisfies strong authentication requirements and can be used to onboard other authentication methods, including Passwordless ones such as Microsoft Authenticator or even Windows Hello. A threat actor could use a TAP to register a new authentication method to maintain persistance to an account. Review any TAP creations to ensure they were used legitimately. Ref: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/security-operations-privileged-accounts#changes-to-privileged-accounts

RuleName: AADR-005 - Bulk Export of Group or Users from Microsoft Entra ID
Description: The rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID audit logs to detect when a bulk export of groups or users is initiated and completed. A bulk export operation allows large-scale extraction of data, such as user or group information, from Microsoft Entra ID. Monitoring this activity is crucial because unauthorized or suspicious bulk data exports can lead to sensitive information leakage or data theft. Malicious actors may attempt to exploit these bulk export operations to gain unauthorized access to large sets of user or group data, potentially compromising the organization's security. The alert records: - Start and End Times of the export operation - Export type (Group Export or User Export) - Initiator's User Principal Name (UPN), User ID, and IP Address - Result and result descriptions of the operation - Correlation ID linking start and finish events The rule helps to promptly detect, analyze, investigate, and respond to unauthorized or suspicious bulk export activities, allowing security teams to mitigate the risk of data exfiltration. Monitoring bulk exports in Microsoft Entra ID is crucial for ensuring security, preventing data breaches, supporting compliance audits, and maintaining control over sensitive information access. This enables organizations to identify unauthorized activities, manage permissions, and improve overall data security.

RuleName: AADR-006 - Authentication Methods Changed for Account
Description: This rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID AuditLogs to detect successful changes to authentication methods for user accounts. The detection focuses on authentication method registration, default security information changes, and administrator-driven security information updates. The rule normalizes registered authentication method details from the audit event and distinguishes between privileged and regular accounts using Microsoft Entra ID role assignments, privileged account naming conventions, and the PrivilegedAccounts watchlist. To reduce false positives, the rule excludes selected expected authentication method changes for non-privileged accounts, such as MFA enrollment enforcement and administrator-required MFA re-registration scenarios. Privileged accounts are always included when matching activity is observed. Alert records: - Time when the authentication method change was observed. - Target account and target account ID. - Whether the target account is considered privileged. - Operation name and result reason. - Normalized registered authentication method. - Initiator identity, initiator type, and initiator IP address when available. - CorrelationId for related audit activity lookup. Authentication method changes can be legitimate, but they may also indicate account compromise or persistence activity if an attacker registers or modifies authentication methods to maintain access, bypass expected controls, or prepare for unauthorized sign-ins.

RuleName: AADR-007 - Brute force attack against cloud app
Description: The rule analyzes Microsoft Entra ID (AAD) Sign-in Logs to detect potential brute force attacks on user accounts. It monitors incorrect login attempts (with a threshold set to 5) and tracks subsequent actions after a successful login within a specified time window (threshold of 20 minutes). - If the subsequent action is 'Login Successful,' an alert is triggered, indicating a potentially successful attack. - If the sign-in attempt was blocked by Conditional Access or failed due to unmet MFA requirements, an alert is generated for a potentially unsuccessful attack, which may still indicate a compromise of user credentials. **Alert records:** - Time: The timestamp of the sign-in attempt. - User Principal Name: The username (email) of the account that attempted to sign in. - IP Address: The IP address from which the sign-in attempt was made. - Location: The geographical location associated with the IP address. - Sign-in Status: Whether the sign-in attempt was successful, blocked, or failed. - Failure Reason: If the sign-in attempt failed, the reason for the failure (e.g., incorrect password, MFA required). - Device Information: Details about the device used for the sign-in attempt. - App Name: The application or service the user was trying to access. - Conditional Access Policy: Any conditional access policies that were applied during the sign-in attempt.
Req. modification: all optionally AAD reg device TrustedLocation Failure threshold time window.

RuleName: AADR-008 - Microsoft Entra ID Role Definition Change Activity
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AuditLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to detect changes to role definitions. It monitors activities categorized under RoleManagement and tracks operations such as Add role definition, Update role definition, and Delete role definition. Modifications to role definitions such as creating, updating, or removing roles, can significantly affect access control within the organization. Unauthorized or misconfigured role changes can lead to privilege escalation, excessive permissions, or disruption of enforcement policies. This rule is designed to capture key details of role definition activity, including the user performing the change, the role affected, and the originating IP address and location. Monitoring these events provides visibility into administrative configuration changes and ensures governance over identity and access privileges. Alert Records: - Time: Timestamp of the role definition change. - Caller: UPN and object ID of the identity that initiated the change. - Operation: Type of action performed (Created, Updated, Deleted). - Role Details: Name, ID, and property metadata of the modified role. - Location: IP address and geographic location (country and city) of the caller. Monitoring role definition changes in Microsoft Entra ID is critical for ensuring the integrity of privileged access management and detecting potential misuse of administrative rights.

RuleName: AADR-009 - External guest invitation followed by Microsoft Entra ID PowerShell signin
Description: By default guests have capability to invite more external guest users, guests also can do suspicious Microsoft Entra ID enumeration. This detection look at guests users, who have been invited or have invited recently, who also are logging via various PowerShell CLI. Ref : 'https://danielchronlund.com/2021/11/18/scary-azure-ad-tenant-enumeration-using-regular-b2b-guest-accounts/

RuleName: AADR-010 - Changes to PIM Settings
Description: PIM provides a key mechanism for assigning privileges to accounts, this query detects changes to PIM role settings. Monitor these changes to ensure they are being made legitimately and don't confer more privileges than expected or reduce the security of a PIM elevation. Ref: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/security-operations-privileged-accounts#changes-to-privileged-accounts

RuleName: AADR-011 - Log4j vulnerability exploit aka Log4Shell IP IOC
Description: Identifies a match across various data feeds for IP IOCs related to the Log4j vulnerability exploit aka Log4Shell described in CVE-2021-44228. References: https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=2021-44228

RuleName: AADR-012 - Member Assigned to Microsoft Cloud Privileged Group
Description: This rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID AuditLogs to identify successful member or owner assignments to privileged cloud groups. The rule detects GroupManagement operations where a user, group, service principal, device, or other object is added as a member or owner to a group considered privileged. A group is treated as privileged when its object ID is listed in the EntraIdPrivilegedGroups watchlist or when its display name matches the configured privileged group naming convention. Alert records: - Time when the assignment was observed. - Assigned target object type, name, and object ID. - Privileged group name and object ID. - Caller identity and caller IP address. - Assignment type and related service context, where available. - Assigned role metadata from the watchlist, where available. Privileged cloud groups may grant access to Microsoft Entra roles, Azure roles, administrative applications, Intune, Azure SQL, Azure Key Vault, third-party applications, or other sensitive resources. Unauthorized membership or ownership changes may create privilege escalation, persistence, or lateral movement opportunities and should be reviewed promptly.

RuleName: Membership has been assigned to group via PIM
Description: The rule detect when the membership has been assigned to group via PIM. Be sure to verify this is an expected addition.

RuleName: AADR-013 - MFA Disabled for a User
Description: The rule evaluates attempts to disable MFA on a user account, assuming that MFA is enabled on a per-user basis, meaning MFA is not enforced through Conditional Access policies. The rule records the target account, initiator account, result status, and other details. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) helps prevent credential compromise.

RuleName: AADR-014 - Microsoft Entra ID Application ID URI Changed
Description: The rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID audit logs and detects when someone changes the Microsoft Entra ID Application ID URI. AppID URIs are fundamental components of security in many applications, especially those utilizing OAuth or other authentication mechanisms. Monitoring modifications ensures compliance with security standards and best practices. The alert records relevant and available details for analysis: - Application name, Object ID, and Client ID - Old URI value, New URI value - Initiator, Initiator ID, and Initiator IP Address Monitoring AppID URI modifications is essential for maintaining the security, integrity, and compliance of applications, helping organizations prevent unauthorized access, mitigate risks, and uphold best practices in information security.

RuleName: AADR-015 - Microsoft Entra ID Application registered
Description: The rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID audit logs and detects application registration events. Rapid detection of suspicious app registration activities can aid in early identification and mitigation of security threats, such as malicious actors attempting to create backdoor access or exploit vulnerabilities within the M365 environment. The alert records relevant and available details for analysis: - Registered application name, Object ID, and Client ID - Initiator, Initiator ID, and Initiator IP Address In summary, monitoring app registration events in Microsoft Entra ID is a critical security measure that helps organizations maintain control over their application landscape, mitigate security risks, and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

RuleName: AADR-016 - Microsoft Entra ID Break Glass Account Logon Monitoring
Description: This detection rule is designed to monitor logon activity related to Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Break glass accounts. These accounts are typically used in emergency situations when normal administrative accounts are unavailable or compromised. If any such activity is detected for any break glass accounts, an alert is triggered to allow security teams to investigate and respond appropriately. By monitoring break glass account activity, this rule helps ensure that these privileged accounts are used only when necessary and in accordance with established security policies.

RuleName: AADR-017 - Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access Policy Activity Monitoring
Description: This rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID audit events from the AuditLogs table to identify successful Conditional Access policy changes, including policy creation, deletion, enablement, disablement, report-only mode changes, grant control changes, application exclusions, platform conditions, user/group/role scope changes, and policy name changes. The rule parses the changed Conditional Access policy object from TargetResources and classifies the policy activity based on the previous and new policy configuration. It also enriches the alert with the most recent sign-in context for the same initiator and IP address when available. Alert records include: - Time when the Conditional Access policy change occurred. - Initiator that performed the change. - Initiator type, user or application. - Source IP address and derived location. - Conditional Access policy name and policy ID. - Classified Conditional Access policy activity. - Sign-in Conditional Access status and device context, when available. - Detection reason explaining the policy change. Conditional Access policies enforce important access controls such as MFA, device compliance, application scope, platform conditions, and user or group targeting. Unauthorized or unexpected changes may weaken identity protections, bypass security requirements, or reduce enforcement coverage across Microsoft Entra ID protected resources.

RuleName: AADR-018 - Microsoft Entra ID PowerShell accessing non-AAD resources
Description: This will alert when a user or application signs in using Microsoft Entra ID PowerShell to access non-Active Directory resources, such as the Azure Key Vault, which may be undesired or unauthorized behavior. For capabilities and expected behavior of the Microsoft Entra ID PowerShell module, see: https://docs.microsoft.com/powershell/module/azuread/?view=azureadps-2.0. For further information on Microsoft Entra ID Signin activity reports, see: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/reports-monitoring/concept-sign-ins.

RuleName: AADR-019 - Microsoft Entra ID Privileged Account updated
Description: The rule detects events when anyone update the Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Privileged Account. The update of a Privileged Account should be rare event and should always be preceded by a request in the form of a ticket. Usually only user administrator or other global administrator can update such properties. Investigate if such user change is an attempt to elevate an existing low privileged identity or rogue administrator activity.

RuleName: AADR-020 - Microsoft Entra ID Role Assignment
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the AuditLogs table to identify role assignments in Microsoft Entra ID, including both traditional IAM operations and Privileged Identity Management (PIM) activity. It detects when roles are assigned to users, service principals, devices, or groups either permanently or temporarily. Monitoring the assignment of privileged roles is crucial, as these permissions can grant access to sensitive systems, administrative capabilities, and escalation vectors. Adversaries or misconfigurations may exploit such assignments to gain or maintain elevated access. Alert Records: - Time: When the role assignment occurred. - Target: Type, name, and ID of the entity receiving the role (user, group, service principal, or device). - Role Details: Name, ID, severity classification, and origin (IAM or PIM). - Caller: Identity and IP address of the user or app that assigned the role. - Location: Country and city from which the assignment was made. - Activity Type: Whether the role was assigned via IAM or PIM, and its context. Identifying and responding to privileged role assignments in Microsoft Entra ID is essential for maintaining a secure identity governance model and preventing abuse of elevated permissions.

RuleName: AADR-021 - Multiple Admins Removed from Roles
Description: The rule evaluates audit events that indicate the removal of roles from multiple accounts (threshold 2) within the Azure and Microsoft Entra ID (AAD) environments in a short time frame (threshold 1h). Its purpose is to identify potentially unauthorized or suspicious activities associated with role removal, where such actions might be an attempt by attackers to lock down the organization and maintain exclusive access. The rule evaluates the removal of any role in the AAD or Azure environment, regardless of its criticality. However, special attention should be given to certain critical roles, such as Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Owner, User Access Administrator, etc. These roles should be prioritized in the analysis due to their significance. The alert records the initiator of the operation, including IP address, environment, number of targets, target accounts, and other relevant information.

RuleName: AADR-022 - Multiple Password Reset in AD or MS Entra ID
Description: This rule is designed to evaluate situations where there are multiple consecutive password resets in Active Directory (AD) or Microsoft Entra ID (AAD). The rule defines various parameters and limitations, such as the maximum number of password resets per user, overall limit for all users (threshlods) and exceptions for specific approved accounts. The rule generates alerts containing information about the start and end times of the monitored period, the number of password resets, user accounts, and computers where the resets occurred. Alerts are further categorized into "Per User Reset" (password resets for individual users) and "Total User Reset" (the overall number of password resets exceeding the defined limit). The rule serves to identify potentially risky situations where unauthorized password resets may occur in the Active Directory or Microsoft Entra ID environment.

RuleName: AADR-023 - New IsAssignableToRole group has been created in Microsoft Entra ID
Description: New Azure AD group with the ‘isAssignableToRole’ property set to True has been created. This attribute allows assign group to the role. Assign role over this hidden from your default monitoring. Please verify that this group is created correctly, as well as any subsequent actions on this group.

RuleName: AADR-024 - Password Cracking Attempts in Microsoft Entra ID
Description: The rule evaluates interactive sign-in logs in Microsoft Entra ID to detect password cracking attempts. The rule monitors an unusually high number of failed password attempts coming from multiple IP addresses and countries for a user account where the device is unmanaged. This rule effectively detects unsuccessful identity attacks. These error codes are included: - 50053: Account is locked because the user tried to sign in too many times with an incorrect user ID or password. - 50055: Invalid password, entered expired password. - 50056: Invalid or null password - Password does not exist in the store for this user. - 50126: Invalid username or password, or invalid on-premises username or password. If such activity is detected, an alert is created and records: - Start and End Times - User Principal Name - Count of Failed Sign-ins - Count of Unique Locations and set of Locations - Count of Unique IPs and set of IP addresses - Applications - Result Descriptions Monitoring these activities is crucial for security as it helps identify and mitigate potential unauthorized access attempts. By detecting and responding to password cracking attempts, we can protect user accounts and sensitive data from being compromised.

RuleName: AADR-025 - Password Reset of Microsoft Entra ID Privileged Account
Description: The rule detects events when anyone reset the password of Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Privileged Account. The password reset of a Privileged Account should be rare event and should always be preceded by a request in the form of a ticket.

RuleName: AADR-026 - Permissions Granted to Microsoft Entra ID Application
Description: The rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID audit logs and detects successful changes when Permissions or Delegated Permissions (Admin Consent) are Granted to Application (Service Principal). This can help identify applications that have been abused to gain unapproved access, for example, read and manage the role-based access control (RBAC) settings for the directory (RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory). The alert records relevant and available details for analysis: - Operation (Permission Grant or Admin Consent or App role assignment to service principal) - Application name - App Service Principal ID - Granted permissions - Previously granted permission - Initiator, Initiator ID, and Initiator IP Address Monitoring permission changes in applications is a critical aspect of maintaining a secure and compliant IT environment. Unauthorized or inappropriate permission grants can lead to potential security breaches, where sensitive data might be accessed, altered, or deleted. By keeping a close eye on permission changes, we can detect any unusual or suspicious activity early and take appropriate action. This can prevent potential exploitation of application permissions, ensuring that only approved and necessary access is granted. Furthermore, this monitoring aids in maintaining compliance with various IT regulations and standards, which often require detailed auditing of permission changes. Therefore, this rule not only enhances security but also contributes to the overall governance and compliance efforts of your organization.

RuleName: AADR-027 - PIM Alert Manipulation Detection
Description: The rules evaluate audit logs from Microsoft Entra ID (AAD) to detect activities related to deactivation and turning off alerting in Privileged Identity Management (PIM). PIM generates alerts when there is suspicious or unsafe activity in your environment. Turning off alerting services or deactivating generated alerts may represent an attempt to conceal unauthorized or suspicious activities in the environment. If such an event is detected, rules will record the initiator, type of activity, and relevant alerts.

RuleName: AADR-028 - Possible MFA Bombing in Microsoft Entra ID
Description: The rule identifies potential MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) bombing attempts, where a user explicitly rejects or does not respond to MFA notifications, indicating that the login attempt was unexpected and that the user's account credentials might be compromised. The rule triggers when more than two (threshold) MFA denial events occur within an hour. It analyzes Microsoft Entra ID (AAD) Sign-In logs to detect specific MFA denial responses and correlates this data with device fingerprints, conditional access status, and geographical locations. If a user repeatedly denies or ignores MFA requests, it raises an alert for further investigation. Alert records: - User Principal Name and User ID - Location - IP Address - Conditional Access Status - Correlation ID Monitoring for potential MFA bombing attempts is crucial because such activities can indicate that an attacker is attempting to gain unauthorized access to user accounts. By detecting and investigating repeated MFA denials, security teams can identify compromised accounts and take necessary actions to prevent unauthorized access. This proactive approach helps in mitigating risks associated with credential theft and enhances the overall security posture of the organization.

RuleName: AADR-029 - Successful Sign-ins from IPs with Failed Attempts on Disabled Accounts
Description: The rule detects potentially suspicious IP addresses that successfully sign in to accounts after attempting to access disabled accounts, a behavior indicative of possible malicious activity targeting disabled users. It leverages Microsoft Entra ID (AAD) Sign-In and AAD Non-Interactive Sign-In logs to analyze sign-in patterns. The rule specifically monitors IP addresses that attempt logins to disabled accounts (error code 50057) and then achieve successful sign-ins to other accounts, excluding those IPs from a predefined watchlist of known safe IPs. Key detection steps: - Identify IP addresses that repeatedly attempt sign-ins to disabled accounts. - Filter successful sign-ins from these IP addresses, counting unique users and applications accessed. - Enrich results with behavioral analytics insights to reduce false positives by assessing related user and device activity and assigning an investigation priority score. - Calculate the Success-Fail Ratio (SFRatio) to prioritize IP addresses where attempts to access disabled accounts comprise at least 50% of logins, signaling potentially risky IP behavior. Alert records: - IP Address and Location - Total attempts to disabled accounts - Number of unique disabled accounts targeted - Set of successfully accessed accounts and applications By identifying IPs with high SFRatio and correlating this with device and user insights, the rule highlights accounts or IP addresses potentially associated with unauthorized access attempts, allowing security teams to investigate and respond to these suspicious activities effectively. This approach enhances proactive defense against account compromise and unauthorized access attempts targeting disabled accounts.

RuleName: AADR-030 - Suspicious application consent similar to O365 Attack Toolkit
Description: This will alert when a user consents to provide a previously-unknown Azure application with the same OAuth permissions used by the MDSec O365 Attack Toolkit (https://github.com/mdsecactivebreach/o365-attack-toolkit). The default permissions/scope for the MDSec O365 Attack toolkit change sometimes but often include contacts.read, user.read, mail.read, notes.read.all, mailboxsettings.readwrite, files.readwrite.all, mail.send, files.read, and files.read.all. Consent to applications with these permissions should be rare, especially as the knownApplications list is expanded, especially as the knownApplications list is expanded. For further information on AuditLogs please see https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/reports-monitoring/reference-audit-activities.

RuleName: AADR-031 - Suspicious application consent similar to PwnAuth
Description: This will alert when a user consents to provide a previously-unknown Azure application with the same OAuth permissions used by the FireEye PwnAuth toolkit (https://github.com/fireeye/PwnAuth). The default permissions/scope for the PwnAuth toolkit are user.read, offline_access, mail.readwrite, mail.send, and files.read.all. Consent to applications with these permissions should be rare, especially as the knownApplications list is expanded. For further information on AuditLogs please see https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/reports-monitoring/reference-audit-activities.

RuleName: AADR-032 - Suspicious Service Principal creation activity
Description: This alert will detect creation of an SPN, permissions granted, credentials created, activity and deletion of the SPN in a time frame (default 10 minutes)

RuleName: AADR-033 - Suspicious Sign-in activity of MS Entra ID Identity
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the SigninLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to identify suspicious sign-in activities. The rule analyzes a combination of behavior patterns related to successful user logins, including: - Four or fewer active login days from a given location during the selected time window. - Sign-ins from a country that is not the user’s most frequently logged-in country. - Changes in device fingerprints between consecutive logins. - High-speed travel between login locations, exceeding a threshold of 300 km/h (configurable). - Logins from IP addresses that are not listed in a watchlist of known IPs or subnets. These patterns align with potential adversarial techniques described in the MITRE ATT&CK framework, specifically within the Credential Access tactic. The relevant technique is T1078 - Valid Accounts, where attackers leverage stolen or misused credentials to gain unauthorized access to systems or services. By identifying deviations in login behavior, geographic anomalies, and device inconsistencies, this rule aims to detect early signs of account compromise or misuse, which could lead to data breaches or lateral movement within the environment. Alert records: - A user logs in from a location or country that deviates from their typical behavior. - The login originates from an IP address not included in the organization's allowlist or known subnets. - The device used for login is non-compliant or exhibits changes in its fingerprint. - The login involves unrealistic travel speeds between consecutive locations. Monitoring such events is critical for detecting and mitigating risks associated with account compromise and unauthorized access, as these behaviors often indicate malicious activity targeting valid user accounts.

RuleName: AADR-034 - User added to Azure AD Privileged Groups outside of PIM
Description: This will alert when a user is added to any of the Privileged Groups outside of PIM. For further information on AuditLogs please see https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/reports-monitoring/reference-audit-activities. For Administrator role permissions in Azure Active Directory please see https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/users-groups-roles/directory-assign-admin-roles

RuleName: AADR-035 - User State changed from Guest to Member
Description: Detects when a guest account in a tenant is converted to a member of the tenant. Monitoring guest accounts and the access they are provided is important to detect potential account abuse. Accounts converted to members should be investigated to ensure the activity was legitimate. Ref: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/security-operations-user-accounts#monitoring-for-failed-unusual-sign-ins

RuleName: AADR-036 - Owner Added to Microsoft Entra ID Application
Description: The rule evaluates Microsoft Entra ID audit logs and detects when a Owner of an Application is added. An owner of an application in Microsoft Entra ID manages app-specific settings like single sign-on, provisioning, and user assignments. Owners can also add or remove other owners but only for applications they own. An attacker can exploit the assignment of an application owner in Entra ID by impersonating the owner to gain access to sensitive data, change permissions, or misuse access rights to obtain protected information or perform malicious operations. The alert records relevant and available details for analysis: - Date and Time - Application name, Object ID, AppId - Target owner info - Initiator, Initiator ID, and Initiator IP Address - Result, etc. The rule allows us to promptly detect, analyze, investigate, and respond to unauthorized changes, helping to prevent unauthorized access and potential security breaches. Monitoring the assignment of an application owner in Entra ID is crucial for security, access management, auditing, and process optimization. It helps identify unauthorized changes, manage permissions, provide audit evidence, and improve the efficiency of application management.

RuleName: AADR-037 - New Domain Added to Microsoft Entra Tenant
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AuditLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to identify instances where a new domain is added to the tenant. The detection includes both verified and unverified domains. Attackers or unauthorized insiders may add malicious or unauthorized domains to the tenant in an attempt to perform phishing attacks, bypass email security mechanisms, or set up deceptive environments for lateral movement and data exfiltration. Monitoring such events aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK framework, helping organizations mitigate risks associated with domain-based attacks. Alert Records: - Time: Timestamp of when the domain was added. - Domain Added: The name of the newly added domain. - Initiator: The identity of the user or service principal that performed the action, including their ID. - IP Address and Location: The IP address and geolocation of the initiator. Monitoring domain additions is essential for maintaining control over your tenant and identifying unauthorized configuration changes that could lead to security breaches.

RuleName: AADR-038 - Activity on AAD Object made by Logic App Identity
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) AuditLogs table to detect activities performed on Azure AD objects by specific identities associated with Logic Apps or automated processes. Such identities (e.g., Azure Logic Apps - Azure AD or specified account UPN) are typically used by Microsoft Sentinel playbooks for automation purposes and should only perform actions within well-defined scopes. This rule detects the following scenarios: - The identity is used by an attacker, indicating potential misuse or compromise. - The identity is used by its designated Logic App, performing an expected operation. - The identity is used by an unauthorized Logic App, suggesting possible misconfiguration or improper usage. Alert Records: - Time: When the activity occurred. - Initiator: The identity responsible for the activity, including user principal name, ID, and IP address. - Target Object: Details of the target object, including its name, ID, and type. - Location: The geographic location derived from the initiator's IP address. - Operation: The type of activity performed on the Azure AD object. Monitoring these activities is critical to ensuring that automation accounts operate within their intended limits, minimizing risks of privilege escalation, misconfiguration, or unauthorized access.

RuleName: AADR-039 - Policy Configuration Changes in Microsoft Entra ID
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AuditLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to identify successful non-Conditional Access policy configuration changes in the Policy category. The rule monitors Update policy operations on Microsoft Entra ID policy objects and excludes Conditional Access policy changes that are covered by the dedicated Conditional Access monitoring rule. It also suppresses generic audit metadata rows and known Microsoft password reset service SPN metadata updates that do not represent actionable policy configuration changes. Alert records: - Time when the policy was updated. - Policy name and policy ID. - Modified property name. - Previous and new values for the updated property. - Initiator that performed the change, including initiator type and ID. - Source IP address, when available. - Correlation ID and original audit context. Changes to identity-related policies may indicate administrative activity, misconfiguration, or unauthorized modification of tenant security controls. Monitoring these changes helps maintain policy governance and supports investigation of unexpected configuration drift outside Conditional Access policy management.

RuleName: AADR-040 - Credential Abuse Blocked by Conditional Access
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the SigninLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to identify potential credential abuse attempts that were blocked by Conditional Access (CA) policies. The rule focuses on successful credential submissions that were ultimately denied access due to Conditional Access enforcement (ResultType 53003). Such events indicate that the credentials were technically valid but failed risk-based evaluation – a common symptom of credential theft or abuse. To reduce noise, the rule filters out trusted IP addresses based on a watchlist and non-critical devices (e.g., compliant corporate assets). Alert Records: - Time: Timestamp of the blocked sign-in attempt. - User: UserPrincipalName and UserId used during the attempt. - IP Address and Location: Source of the login, including city and country. - Application: The application being accessed during the sign-in attempt. - Device: Device OS, compliance status, management status, and trust type. - Failed Policies: Conditional Access policy names that blocked the sign-in. - Privilege: Whether the user has elevated roles assigned. Monitoring these activities supports early detection of account compromise and strengthens the organization’s identity protection strategy.

RuleName: AADR-041 - Privilege Elevation to User Access Administrator in Entra ID
Description: The rule detects the elevation of access permissions to the "User Access Administrator" role at the Microsoft Entra ID tenant level. The "Elevate Access" operation grants significant privileges allowing broad access management across all Azure resources within the tenant. Such an action is typically performed only in exceptional circumstances and should be closely monitored, as unauthorized or malicious usage could lead to privilege escalation, unauthorized access, or compromise of Azure resources. Monitoring these elevations is essential to promptly detect and investigate potential security incidents involving misuse of administrative privileges. Alert Records: -Time: Timestamp of the privilege elevation - Initiator: User principal name or application that initiated the operation - IP Address: Source IP address of the operation - Location: Geographical location determined by the IP address Investigate promptly any elevation to User Access Administrator, ensuring it aligns with authorized administrative tasks.

RuleName: AADR-042 - Pass-the-Cookie Attack in Microsoft 365
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs table to identify potential Pass-the-Cookie activity. The rule focuses on sign-ins via browser-based, non-interactive sessions using the same session ID across significantly different locations and IP addresses. Such activity is commonly associated with session hijacking techniques, where an attacker reuses a legitimate session token (cookie) to authenticate without needing the user's password or MFA. This rule specifically detects rapid changes in geographic location during a single session, using high travel speed (e.g., > 120 km/h), sign-in from unknown or rare IP addresses, and access from previously unseen locations. Alert Records: - Time: Current and previous sign-in timestamps. - Session: Shared session ID across distinct locations. - Location: Current and previous IP address and location information. - Distance & Speed: Calculated travel distance and speed between sign-ins. - User & Application: Affected user, accessed application, and client app used. - Device: Current and previous device name, compliance, and managed state. Detecting session reuse across geographically distant locations helps identify advanced attacks bypassing authentication controls. These attacks are difficult to detect using traditional login anomaly rules and require behavioral correlation across session data.

RuleName: AADR-043 - Legacy Authentication Bypassing MFA and Conditional Access
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to identify successful non-interactive sign-ins performed via legacy authentication protocols. The rule looks for successful authentications where the client application matches common legacy protocols (for example IMAP4, POP3, SMTP, Exchange ActiveSync, Exchange Web Services, and Exchange Online PowerShell). It then aggregates activity per user and application over the last hour and triggers when the number of successful non-interactive sign-ins exceeds a defined threshold (more than 3). Attackers who obtain valid credentials may intentionally use legacy authentication because these protocols are often less capable of enforcing modern controls and may be used to bypass protections such as MFA enforcement and Conditional Access requirements. This can enable unauthorized access to services (commonly email-related workloads) while reducing visibility and friction compared to interactive sign-ins. Alert records: - Time: FirstSeen, LastSeen (time range of the aggregated activity). - User: UserPrincipalName, UserId. - Application: AppDisplayName. - Activity: SignInCount (number of successful non-interactive sign-ins). - Network: IPAddress (representative IP), plus aggregated IPs and Countries. - Protocol: Protocols. We monitor this activity because legacy authentication remains a frequent avenue for account misuse and automation, especially for mailbox access. Elevated volumes of successful non-interactive sign-ins using legacy protocols can indicate credential compromise, insecure client configurations, or unauthorized access paths that should be reduced or blocked to improve identity security posture.

RuleName: AADR-044 - Stale Membership in Temporary Entra ID Groups
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AuditLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to identify cases where a member was added to a temporary Entra ID group but was not removed within the expected time window. The rule monitors successful Add member to group operations for groups classified as temporary (defined via a watchlist) and correlates them with corresponding Remove member from group events. If no removal action is observed after the membership addition, or if the removal occurred before the addition event, the membership is considered stale. Such conditions may result from operational oversight, misconfigured automation, or failures in access governance processes. In more severe scenarios, an attacker or insider with sufficient permissions could intentionally retain group membership to maintain access beyond the approved duration. This activity aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK framework, as maintaining unintended group membership can be used to achieve persistence or privilege escalation by manipulating account permissions. Alert records: - Time: When the group membership was added. - Group: Name and object ID of the temporary Entra ID group. - Target: The user or service principal added to the group. - Initiator: The user or application that performed the membership change. - IP address: Source IP address associated with the add operation. - Correlation ID: Identifier used to correlate related audit events. Monitoring this activity is critical because temporary Entra ID groups are commonly used to grant time-bound or elevated access. Failure to revoke such access increases the risk of unauthorized privilege retention, policy violations, and prolonged exposure of sensitive resources.

RuleName: AADR-045 - Password Spray Attack via Non-Interactive Sign-Ins
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to detect password spray attacks performed through non-interactive authentication attempts. The rule identifies scenarios where a single IP address generates failed sign-in attempts against multiple user accounts within a defined time window using common authentication error codes (e.g., 50034, 50053, 50126), and triggers when the number of targeted accounts exceeds a defined threshold (e.g., more than 10 users or at least 10% of organization members). Password spraying is a credential access technique in which an attacker attempts a small number of commonly used passwords across many accounts to avoid lockouts and evade detection; non-interactive sign-ins are particularly attractive because they may leverage legacy protocols or background authentication flows that are less visible to end users and traditional monitoring controls. Alert records: - Time window: FirstSeen and LastSeen of the activity - Source: IP address and geographic location - Targeted accounts: Number of unique users (TargetCount) - Failure details: Total failed attempts (FailCount) and associated result codes - User agents observed during the activity Monitoring this activity aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1110.003 – Password Spraying and is critical for detecting credential access attempts that may lead to account compromise.

RuleName: AADR-046 - Legacy ROPC Authentication Observed
Description: This rule identifies the use of the Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) OAuth flow in non-interactive sign-ins to Microsoft Entra ID. ROPC is a legacy authentication mechanism in which an application submits the user's username and password directly to the authorization endpoint in order to obtain an access token. This model is considered less secure than modern interactive authentication flows because it requires handling user credentials within the application. ROPC usage may indicate: - A legacy application or integration relying on password-based authentication - An automation script using stored user credentials - Programmatic authentication performed with a user account The presence of this authentication flow should be periodically reviewed and restricted to approved and documented use cases only. Alert records: - Time: When the ROPC sign-in occurred - User: UserPrincipalName and UserId - Application: AppDisplayName - Source: IP address and resolved location - Result: ResultType (successful sign-in) Monitoring this activity is important because ROPC usage can indicate legacy integrations, automation using stored credentials, or potential credential misuse. ROPC should be restricted to approved and documented use cases and reviewed regularly.

RuleName: AADR-047 - Refresh Token Replay from New Locations
Description: This rule analyzes audit events from the AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs table in Microsoft Entra ID to identify high-frequency successful non-interactive authentication activity within a single session (SessionId) observed from multiple countries within the configured time window. The detection identifies scenarios where the same session context is associated with more than one geographic country, which may indicate refresh token replay, session reuse across locations, or unauthorized use of authentication artifacts. To reduce false positives, the detection excludes trusted network locations, known corporate IP ranges, and Microsoft applications that are known to generate high-volume background authentication traffic. Alert records include: - Time window: FirstSeen and LastSeen of the activity - UserPrincipalName and UserId - AppDisplayName - SessionId - Volume of RefreshCount (successful non-interactive authentications) - Countries observed within the session - Source addresses Reuse of the same session across multiple countries within a short period is atypical in standard user behavior and may represent token replay or unauthorized reuse of authentication artifacts, potentially leading to account compromise and unauthorized access to cloud resources.

RuleName: AZUR-001 - Azure Diagnostic Settings Deleted From Resource
Description: The rule evaluates for diagnostic settings that are removed from a resource. This could indicate an attacker or malicious internal trying to evade detection before malicious acts are performed. If the diagnostic settings are being deleted as part of a parent resource deletion, the event is ignored. The resource deleting is monitored by detection rule Cloud resource deletions by User.

RuleName: AZUR-002 - Azure Resource Role Assignment
Description: The rule evaluates events from the AzureActivity and AuditLogs tables to detect the assignment of Azure resource roles, including both standard Identity and Access Management (IAM) operations and Privileged Identity Management (PIM) role activations. Attackers or unauthorized administrators may assign elevated roles to bypass access controls, establish persistence, or access sensitive resources. This rule supports the principle of least privilege and ensures proper visibility into privileged access management. Alert Records: - Time: When the role assignment took place. - Target: Type, name, and ID of the identity receiving the role. - Role Details: Name, ID, severity classification, and source (Azure or Entra ID). - Scope: Scope type and resource associated with the assignment (e.g., Subscription, Resource Group). - Caller: User or application assigning the role, along with their IP address. - Location: Geographic origin of the caller's IP address. - Activity Type: Indicates whether the role was assigned via IAM or PIM and the nature of the operation. Monitoring privileged role assignments across Azure resources is essential for detecting unauthorized privilege elevation, ensuring role governance, and reducing the attack surface for identity-based threats.

RuleName: AZUR-003 - Azure Virtual Network Perring Configuration Activity
Description: The Azure Virtual Network Peering Configuration Activity detection rule is designed to monitor and alert on any successful ‘Write’ operations performed on Azure Virtual Network Peering. These operations could potentially indicate changes in the network infrastructure, which might have implications for security, performance, or functionality. Virtual Network Peering can serve as a router and open a pathway to your environment even from another tenant (Cross-tenant peering). Configurations of VNet peering appear very rarely and should always be supported by an appropriate change request. The alert records include the following details: - Time: The timestamp of the activity. - Resource Details: Information about the resource, including type, name, id, resource group, and subscription id. - Caller Details: Information about the caller, including type, name, id, IP address, and role. - Properties, Authorization, Claims: Additional details about the operation. - Location Details: Geographical information related to the operation. - Correlation Id: A unique identifier for the operation. Monitoring such activities can help in maintaining the security and integrity of the network infrastructure.

RuleName: AZUR-004 - Azure VM Run Command linked with MDE
Description: Identifies any Azure VM Run Command operations and links these operations with MDE host logging. Linking these two data sources provides hunting opportunities. Logging from AzureActivity provides the IP address and UPN of the account that invoked the command. Joining this with logging from MDE provides insights into what cmdlets were loaded by the command.

RuleName: AZUR-005 - Azure VM Run Command operation executed during suspicious login window
Description: Identifies when the Azure Run Command operation is executed by a UserPrincipalName and IP Address that has resulted in a recent user entity behaviour alert.

RuleName: AZUR-006 - Azure VM Run Command operations executing a unique PowerShell script
Description: This rule evaluates AzureActivity logs to detect the use of Azure Run Command for executing PowerShell scripts on virtual machines. It correlates these logs with DeviceFileEvents and DeviceEvents to track the creation and execution of PowerShell scripts. The uniqueness of the PowerShell script is determined by hashing the cmdlets called within the script and its file size. Attackers or insiders may use Azure Run Command to execute unauthorized or malicious PowerShell scripts on virtual machines. Detecting unique or rare scripts can help identify unusual activity that deviates from typical administrative behavior, potentially indicating attempts to establish persistence, escalate privileges, or compromise resources. Rule Name Suggestions: Unique PowerShell Script Executed via Azure VM Run Command Uncommon PowerShell Run Command Execution on Virtual Machine Azure VM Run Command - Unique PowerShell Script Execution Rare PowerShell Execution via Azure Run Command Unique PowerShell Run Detected on Azure Virtual Machine Rule Description: This rule evaluates AzureActivity logs to detect the use of Azure Run Command for executing PowerShell scripts on virtual machines. It correlates these logs with DeviceFileEvents and DeviceEvents to track the creation and execution of PowerShell scripts. The uniqueness of the PowerShell script is determined by hashing the cmdlets called within the script and its file size. Attackers or insiders may use Azure Run Command to execute unauthorized or malicious PowerShell scripts on virtual machines. Detecting unique or rare scripts can help identify unusual activity that deviates from typical administrative behavior, potentially indicating attempts to establish persistence, escalate privileges, or compromise resources. Alert Records: - Start Time: The start time of the Azure Run Command activity. - End Time: The end time of the Azure Run Command activity. - PowerShell File Name: The name of the PowerShell script executed. - Virtual Machine: The name of the affected virtual machine. - Caller: The user or process responsible for executing the PowerShell script. - Caller IP Address: The IP address from which the Run Command was executed. - PowerShell Script Commands: The cmdlets called within the PowerShell script. - PowerShell File Size: The size of the PowerShell script file. - Prevalence: A percentage indicating how often this script has been observed in the environment. Monitoring unique PowerShell scripts executed via Azure Run Command is essential for detecting potential threats, ensuring accountability, and identifying deviations from normal operational activity.

RuleName: AZUR-007 - BYOK Enabled on Storage Account or Disk
Description: The rule is designed to monitor and alert on activities related to the enablement of Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) on Azure Storage or VM Disk. BYOK is a feature that allows you to control and manage the key used for disk encryption. While this is a legitimate operation, it can pose a potential security risk if it's not part of your organization's policy or if it's performed by an unauthorized user. When the rule detects any of the mentioned activities, it generates one of the following alerts: - BYOK Enabled on Azure Storage Account - BYOK Enabled on Azure Disk The alert records include the following details: - Time: The timestamp of the activity. - Resource Details: Information about the resource, including type, name, id, resource group, and subscription id. - Caller Details: Information about the caller, including type, name, id, IP address, and role. - BYOK Properties: Specific properties related to the BYOK operation. - Properties, Authorization, Claims: Additional details about the operation. - Location Details: Geographical information related to the operation. - Encryption Details: Information about the encryption, including type, key source, key name, disk encryption set id, and user-assigned identity. - Correlation Id: A unique identifier for the operation. These alerts are designed to provide comprehensive visibility into BYOK-related activities in your Azure environment, helping you maintain security and compliance. If you receive such an alert, it's important to verify whether the activity was expected and authorized. If not, it may indicate a potential security issue that needs to be addressed. Always follow your organization's policy and procedures when responding to such alerts.

RuleName: AZUR-008 - Cloud resource deletions by User
Description: The rule detects cloud resource deletions by an individual user. These deletions from unusual or privileged users could be an indication of a cloud infrastructure takedown by an adversary. Resources for Microsoft Sentinel are monitored under a different rule and are not included in this rule.

RuleName: AZUR-009 - Creation of expensive VMs in Azure Cloud
Description: The rule evaluates audit records at the Subscription level and detects the creation of large-size virtual machines (with GPU or a significant number of virtual CPUs) in Azure, i.e., very expensive VMs. The initiator may create new or update existing virtual machine sizes to circumvent defenses or use them for cryptocurrency mining purposes. The link below provides a preview of prices for individual VM sizes in various regions. https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/virtual-machines/windows/

RuleName: AZUR-010 - Azure Role Definition Change Activity
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the AzureActivity table to detect changes to Azure role definitions. It monitors successful operations such as roleDefinitions/write and roleDefinitions/delete, identifying role creation, updates, and deletions performed within Azure subscriptions. Unauthorized modifications to role definitions may introduce misconfigured permissions, weaken access control, or allow for privilege escalation. Monitoring these changes is essential to protect sensitive resources and ensure that role management aligns with organizational policies and least-privilege principles. Alert Records: - Time: When the role definition activity was successfully performed. - Operation: Activity type (Created, Updated, Deleted). - Role Details: Role name, ID, description, permissions, and assignable scope. - Caller: Principal identity, type, and role of the initiator. - Location: IP address and geolocation (country and city) from which the activity originated. - Subscription and Resource Context: Azure resource ID, subscription ID, and resource group involved. Monitoring Azure role definition changes is critical for detecting configuration drift, unauthorized privilege changes, and ensuring adherence to governance standards.

RuleName: AZUR-011 - Detection of LA Workspace Deletion and Data Purge
Description: The rule evaluates audit logs at the Subscription level associated with the Log Analytics Workspace. The rule detects Data Purge activities or attempts to delete workspaces within the Log Analytics environment. Workspace deletion alerts help identify potential malicious actions, where attackers may seek to disrupt services by deleting workspaces after compromise or selectively deleting specific data from LA. These operations require critical permissions and are very rare. It is important to note that data purges are not immediate operations and can take hours to days, necessitating a prompt examination of the affected data and consideration of creating backups if the action is deemed unauthorized. The alert records details about the Caller and the used IP address, Log Analytics Workspace Name, and the entire scope (resource), including the table in LA where data deletion is occurring. This dual-focused rule enhances overall security by addressing various threats to the Log Analytics workspace.

RuleName: AZUR-012 - Detection of previously unseen Azure Subscription
Description: The rule detects events from a previously unseen Azure Subscription. This event may indicate the creation of a new Subscription or starting to collect audit events from a subscription to Log Analytics. Enter the SubscriptionID and Subscription Name into the watchlist "SubscriptionList" for subsequent correlation options.

RuleName: AZUR-013 - IP Forwarding Enabled on Azure Network Interface
Description: The rule is designed to identify whether IP Forwarding is enabled on an Azure Network Interface (NIC). IP forwarding is a crucial process that facilitates the routing of IP packets from one router to another until they reach their intended destination. Ensuring the correct configuration of IP forwarding is essential to prevent vulnerabilities in network traffic and unauthorized forwarding. Incorrect settings may expose the network to unwanted traffic, potentially compromising security. Adherence to security protocols and continuous monitoring of IP forwarding activities is crucial. Monitoring allows for the prompt detection of unusual or potentially harmful activities associated with IP forwarding, enabling swift responses to anomalies and potential threats. Alert records: - Information about the Caller, such as ID and IP. - Resource and Resource ID. - Configuration properties, such as IP configuration.

RuleName: AZUR-014 - Multi-user authorization protection Disabled for Azure Backup
