Description: The rule evaluates operations at the subscription level (Azure Activity) and reveals successful disabling of Multi-user authorization (MUA) protection for Azure Backup. For MUA, Azure Backup uses the Resource Guard as an additional authorization mechanism for a Recovery Services vault or a Backup vault, to ensure critical operations are performed only with applicable authorization. Alert is generated if operation "backupResourceGuardProxies" is detected. Alert records: - Information about the Caller, such as ID and IP. - Resource and Resource ID. Disabling Multi-user authorization (MUA) can pose a security risk. This operation is rare and should practically never occur in the environment. Ref: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/multi-user-authorization?tabs=azure-portal&pivots=vaults-recovery-services-vault

RuleName: AZUR-015 - New CloudShell User
Description: Identifies when a user creates an Azure CloudShell for the first time. Monitor this activity to ensure only the expected users are using CloudShell.

RuleName: AZUR-016 - Rare subscription-level operations in Azure
Description: This query looks for a few sensitive subscription-level events based on Azure Activity Logs. For example this monitors for the operation name 'Create or Update Snapshot' which is used for creating backups but could be misused by attackers to dump hashes or extract sensitive information from the disk.

RuleName: AZUR-017 - Suspicious Activity on Azure Policy
Description: This rule evaluates AzureActivity logs to identify successful suspicious or sensitive changes related to Azure Policy. The rule detects Azure Policy assignment deletion, Azure Policy assignment update or replacement patterns, Azure Policy exemption creation, and Azure Policy exclusion creation. Assignment update activity is identified when a policy assignment is deleted and then recreated with the same policy name in the same subscription within a short correlation window. Standalone policy assignment write operations without a matching delete event and without notScopes are not alerted. Alert records: - Time when the Azure Policy activity occurred. - Activity type and dynamic alert name. - Azure Policy name and related policy definition ID. - Deleted assignment, new assignment, exclusion ID, or exemption ID when available. - Subscription, resource group, and resource ID. - Caller identity, caller type, caller role, and source IP address. - Detection reason explaining why the activity was classified. These activities may indicate unauthorized or unexpected changes to Azure Policy governance controls. Policy assignment deletion, replacement, exemptions, or exclusions can weaken security and compliance enforcement and should normally be associated with an approved change request.

RuleName: AZUR-018 - Suspicious number of resource creation or deployment activities
Description: Indicates when an anomalous number of VM creations or deployment activities occur in Azure via the AzureActivity log. The anomaly detection identifies activities that have occurred both since the start of the day 1 day ago and the start of the day 7 days ago. The start of the day is considered 12am UTC time.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Administrator Group Monitoring
Description: This detection monitors for additions to projects or project collection administration groups in an Azure DevOps Organization.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Agent Pool Created Then Deleted
Description: As well as adding build agents to an existing pool to execute malicious activity within a pipeline, an attacker could create a complete new agent pool and use this for execution. Azure DevOps allows for the creation of agent pools with Azure hosted infrastructure or self-hosted infrastructure. Given the additional customizability of self-hosted agents this detection focuses on the creation of new self-hosted pools. To further reduce false positive rates the detection looks for pools created and deleted relatively quickly (within 7 days by default), as an attacker is likely to remove a malicious pool once used in order to reduce/remove evidence of their activity.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Build Variable Modified by New User
Description: Variables can be configured and used at any stage of the build process in Azure DevOps to inject values. An attacker with the required permissions could modify or add to these variables to conduct malicious activity such as changing paths or remote endpoints called during the build. As variables are often changed by users, just detecting these changes would have a high false positive rate. This detection looks for modifications to variable groups where that user has not been observed modifying them before.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Personal Access Token used
Description: The rule evaluate whenever a Personal Access Token (PAT) is used and where is used. PATs are intended for programmatic access use in code or applications and should not be normaly used in Browsers. PAT used in browser could be an indicator of an attacker using a stolen PAT. A PAT identifies you, your accessible organizations, and scopes of access. PAT contains your security credentials and can be used as an alternate password to authenticate into Azure DevOps, so you should treat them the same way. This can be prone to attacker theft if not adequately secured.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Pipeline Created and Deleted on the Same Day
Description: An attacker with access to Azure DevOps could create a pipeline to inject artifacts used by other pipelines, or to create a malicious software build that looks legitimate by using a pipeline that incorporates legitimate elements. An attacker would also likely want to cover their tracks once conducting such activity. This query looks for Pipelines created and deleted within the same day, this is unlikely to be legitimate user activity in the majority of cases.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Pipeline modified by a new user
Description: There are several potential pipeline steps that could be modified by an attacker to inject malicious code into the build cycle. A likely attacker path is the modification to an existing pipeline that they have access to. This detection looks for users modifying a pipeline when they have not previously been observed modifying or creating that pipeline before. This query also joins events with data to Azure AD Identity Protection (AAD IdP) in order to show if the user conducting the action has any associated AAD IdP alerts. You can also choose to filter this detection to only alert when the user also has AAD IdP alerts associated with them.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Pull Request Policy Bypassing - Historic allow list
Description: This detection builds an allow list of historic PR policy bypasses and compares to recent history, flagging pull request bypasses that are not manually in the allow list and not historically included in the allow list.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Retention Reduced
Description: AzureDevOps retains items such as run records and produced artifacts for a configurable amount of time. An attacker looking to reduce the footprint left by their malicious activity may look to reduce the retention time for artifacts and runs. This query will look for where retention has been reduced to the minimum level - 1, or reduced by more than half.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Service Connection Abuse
Description: Flags builds/releases that use a large number of service connections if they aren't manually in the allow list. This is to determine if someone is hijacking a build/release and adding many service connections in order to abuse or dump credentials from service connections.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Service Connection Addition/Abuse - Historic allow list
Description: This detection builds an allow list of historic service connection use by Builds and Releases and compares to recent history, flagging growth of service connection use which are not manually included in the allow list and not historically included in the allow list Build/Release runs. This is to determine if someone is hijacking a build/release and adding many service connections in order to abuse or dump credentials from service connections.

RuleName: Azure DevOps Variable Secret Not Secured
Description: Credentials used in the build process may be stored as Azure DevOps variables. To secure these variables they should be stored in KeyVault or marked as Secrets. This detection looks for new variables added with names that suggest they are credentials but where they are not set as Secrets or stored in KeyVault.

RuleName: Extension Added to Azure DevOps
Description: The rule detects if extension is added to Azure DevOps. The rule records an Actor UPN and ID, extension name, publisher etc. An attacker could use a malicious extension to conduct malicious activity.

RuleName: External Upstream Source Added to Azure DevOps Feed
Description: The detection looks for new external sources added to an Azure DevOps feed. An allow list can be customized to explicitly allow known good sources. An attacker could look to add a malicious feed in order to inject malicious packages into a build pipeline.

RuleName: Multiple Approvals by Single Approver for Azure DevOps Release Deployment
Description: The rule evaluates approval processes for software releases in Azure DevOps and identifies situations where a single approver approved multiple times. The rule monitors events of the type "Release.ApprovalCompleted" in the log data of Azure DevOps. If the number of approvals is higher than the number of unique approvers, the rule evaluates this situation as suspicious and incident is generated and records Project, PipelineId, PipelineName, ActorDisplayName, ApprovalTime. Further investigation and corrective actions may be required to address this issue.

RuleName: New Agent Added to Pool by New User or Added to a New OS Type
Description: As seen in attacks such as SolarWinds attackers can look to subvert a build process by controlling build servers. Azure DevOps uses agent pools to execute pipeline tasks. An attacker could insert compromised agents that they control into the pools in order to execute malicious code. This query looks for users adding agents to pools they have not added agents to before, or adding agents to a pool of an OS that has not been added to that pool before. This detection has potential for false positives so has a configurable allow list to allow for certain users to be excluded from the logic.

RuleName: New PA, PCA, or PCAS added to Azure DevOps
Description: In order for an attacker to be able to conduct many potential attacks against Azure DevOps they will need to gain elevated permissions. This detection looks for users being granted key administrative permissions. If the principal of least privilege is applied, the number of users granted these permissions should be small. Note that permissions can also be granted via Azure AD groups and monitoring of these should also be conducted.

RuleName: NRT Azure DevOps Audit Stream Disabled
Description: Azure DevOps allow for audit logs to be streamed to external storage solutions such as SIEM solutions. An attacker looking to hide malicious Azure DevOps activity from defenders may look to disable data streams before conducting activity and then re-enabling the stream after (so as not to raise data threshold-based alarms). Looking for disabled audit streams can identify this activity, and due to the nature of the action its unlikely to have a high false positive rate.

RuleName: BCEN-001 - Missing Business Central Audit Logs
Description: The rule evaluates Business Central logs to detect when no logs have been received from Business Central for a specified duration. The rule analyzes the timestamp of the most recent log event and checks whether the gap exceeds the defined threshold, indicating potential issues with log generation or transmission. If Business Central fails to send logs for an extended period, this could signal a misconfiguration, malfunction, or potential compromise. Monitoring this event helps maintain compliance and ensures that auditing mechanisms are functioning properly, particularly in environments reliant on Business Central for critical business operations. Alert Records: - Time: The time when the last log event was received from Business Central. - Device: The device name, type, and IP address from which the log was generated. - LastLogTime: The timestamp of the last log event. - TimeSinceLastLog: The duration since the last log was received. Monitoring this activity ensures that log transmission from Business Central is continuous and timely, highlighting potential system issues or risks related to audit and monitoring.

RuleName: BCEN-002 - Business Central Permission Assignment
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the BusinessCentral_CL table to identify permission assignments in the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central environment. The rule detects when a user is granted new permissions, including critical roles such as SUPER, which provide broad administrative access. It evaluates who made the change, what permission was assigned, to whom, and in which scope (e.g., environment, company, or organization). Alert Records: - Event Time: When the permission change occurred. - Initiator: The identity of the user who made the change. - Target: The user who received the new permission, including their name and internal ID. - Action: The nature of the change, including the old and new permission values. - Scope: The level or entity (e.g., company, organization) to which the permission applies. Monitoring permission assignments is essential for enforcing least-privilege principles, preventing misuse of elevated access rights, and ensuring that critical roles are assigned only under approved circumstances. This rule aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1098 - Account Manipulation and supports organizational efforts to monitor identity governance within ERP platforms.

RuleName: BCEN-003 - Bulk Removal of User Permissions from Business Central
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the BusinessCentral_CL table to identify situations where permissions are removed from multiple user accounts in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central within a short period. Attackers or malicious insiders may attempt to weaken security controls by removing permissions from several user accounts, including the highly privileged "SUPER" role. Such actions can lead to privilege abuse, operational sabotage, or attempts to evade detection. Alert records: - Start/End: The time interval during which the permissions were removed. - Initiator: The account or identity that performed the permission removals. - Users: Domain, Names and IDs of affected user accounts. - Permission: The type or types of permission removed, including if the "SUPER" role was affected. - UsersRemoved: The number of user accounts with permissions removed. - Operation Duration: How quickly the permissions were removed. Monitoring this activity is critical because the bulk removal of permissions, especially from privileged roles, can undermine organizational security and disrupt business operations.

RuleName: BCEN-004 - Multiple User Accounts Disabled or Deleted in Business Central
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the BusinessCentral_CL table to detect situations where multiple user accounts are deleted or disabled within a short time interval in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. Attackers or malicious insiders may attempt to disrupt operations, cover their tracks, or remove legitimate user access by deleting or disabling a large number of user accounts in rapid succession. Such mass modifications are uncommon in standard administrative workflows and typically indicate misuse of privileged access or an attempt to hinder incident response. Alert records: - Start / End: The time window during which the user accounts were deleted or disabled. - Affected Users: The total number of user accounts impacted by the operation. - User Names / IDs: Details of the affected accounts. - Initiator: The user or process responsible for initiating the action. - Operation Duration: The total time (in seconds) during which the mass action was performed. - Event: The type of action (User Deleted or User Disabled). - Scope: The relevant scope or context within Business Central. Monitoring this activity is critical because a high number of user account deletions or modifications within a short period can seriously impact business operations, disrupt user access, and may indicate a broader security incident. Early detection allows for rapid investigation and remediation.

RuleName: MCOP-001 - Copilot Indirect Prompt Injection
Description: This rule evaluates Microsoft 365 Copilot activity from the CopilotActivity table to identify Copilot interactions where an accessed grounding resource was flagged for indirect prompt injection, also known as cross-prompt injection attack (XPIA). The rule inspects CopilotInteraction records and expands LLMEventData.AccessedResources to detect resources where XPIADetected is true. Alert records: - First and last time when the XPIA-flagged resource access was observed. - Copilot context or named Copilot agent involved in the interaction. - Initiator identity, initiator IP address, location, and IP type. - Copilot thread ID associated with the interaction. - Resource type, resource actions, accessed sites, resource status, and sensitivity label ID. This activity may indicate exposure to grounding content containing instructions intended to manipulate Copilot behavior. The alert does not confirm successful compromise, prompt execution, or data exfiltration, but it should be reviewed by an analyst.

RuleName: MCOP-002 - Copilot Jailbreak Attempt
Description: This rule evaluates Microsoft 365 Copilot activity from the CopilotActivity table to identify Copilot interactions where one or more messages were flagged for a jailbreak attempt. The rule inspects CopilotInteraction records and expands LLMEventData.Messages to detect messages where JailbreakDetected is true. Alert records: - First and last time when the jailbreak signal was observed. - Copilot context or named Copilot agent involved in the interaction. - Initiator identity, initiator IP address, location, and IP type. - Copilot thread ID associated with the interaction. - Number of jailbreak hits, number of prompt hits, and related message IDs. This activity may indicate that an initiator attempted to manipulate Copilot behavior, bypass expected safeguards, or influence the AI system through direct prompt content. The alert should be reviewed by an analyst to determine whether the activity is benign, related to approved testing, or potentially malicious.

RuleName: MCOP-003 - Copilot Broad Enterprise Resource Access
Description: This rule evaluates Microsoft 365 Copilot activity from the CopilotActivity table to identify Copilot interactions where a single thread accessed a broad set of enterprise resources. The rule inspects CopilotInteraction records and evaluates resources listed in LLMEventData.AccessedResources. It focuses on enterprise grounding resources such as Office documents, Teams content, and knowledge search results, while excluding web search results, Outlook content, action records, Office search entry points, and generic hyperlink wrappers. Alert records: - First and last time when the broad enterprise resource access pattern was observed. - Copilot context or named Copilot agent involved in the interaction. - Initiator identity, initiator IP address, location, and IP type. - Copilot thread ID associated with the interaction. - Number of resource accesses, distinct enterprise resources, distinct resource locations, and distinct resource types. - Resource categories, resource locations, resource URLs, resource types, and resource actions involved in the interaction. This activity may indicate broad internal research, preparation of a report, legitimate business activity, or potentially suspicious use of Copilot to enumerate or collect information across enterprise resources. The alert does not confirm data exfiltration, malicious intent, or unauthorized access. It should be reviewed by an analyst in the context of the initiator role, recent sign-in activity, related Copilot security signals, and sensitivity of the accessed resources.

RuleName: FTGT-001 - FortiGate User Group Modification
Description: The rule evaluates logs to monitor modifications on user groups in Fortinet FortiGate devices. It detects the creation, modification, and deletion of user groups, which could indicate administrative changes or unauthorized access attempts. Attackers or malicious insiders may modify user groups to escalate privileges, gain unauthorized access to network resources, or manipulate security policies. By tracking such activity, organizations can ensure proper access control and detect potential security incidents early. Alert Records: - Time: When the group modification occurred. - Initiator: The user or process responsible for the change. - Action: The type of action performed (group creation, modification, or deletion). - Group Name: The name of the affected user group. - Device: The FortiGate device where the change was made, including its version. - Source Process: The process that initiated the change. Monitoring group modifications is essential for maintaining security policies, preventing unauthorized access, and ensuring compliance with organizational access control policies.

RuleName: FTGT-002 - FortiGate Administrator Account Management
Description: The rule evaluates Fortinet logs to detect administrative actions related to system users on Fortigate devices. It focuses on activities involving administrator accounts (system.admin, system.sso-admin, system.api-user) and critical configuration changes. Attackers or malicious insiders could exploit administrative privileges to add, delete, or modify administrator accounts, potentially altering security settings or gaining persistent access to the system. Monitoring these activities aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1098 - Account Manipulation and is crucial for maintaining the security and integrity of network devices. Alert Records: - Time: When the administrative action occurred. - Initiator: The username of the individual who performed the action. - Action: The type of administrative action executed (Add, Delete, Edit). - Target: The Fortigate configuration object or administrator account affected. - Device: The Fortigate device name, version, and product details. Regularly monitoring administrative actions on Fortigate devices is critical for detecting potential threats, preventing unauthorized access, and ensuring compliance with security policies.

RuleName: FTGT-003 - Firewall Configuration Modifications on Fortinet Devices
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the Fortigate_CL table to identify firewall configuration changes on Fortinet devices. It focuses on administrative activities involving the addition, editing, or deletion of firewall objects such as policies, services, and addresses. These modifications are tracked through system log messages (e.g., "Add firewall.", "Edit firewall.", "Delete firewall.") and enriched with contextual data extracted from fields such as cfgpath, cfgobj, and cfgattr. These fields help identify the nature and scope of the configuration change. Attackers or unauthorized administrators may attempt to alter firewall configurations to weaken security controls, allow malicious traffic, or establish persistent access. Such changes can pose serious risks to network integrity and must be carefully monitored. To reduce false positives, this rule excludes changes performed by the FortiManager service account (Fortimanager_Access), which typically synchronizes configurations across managed devices Alert Records: - Time: When the firewall configuration change was detected. - Device: Fortinet appliance name or external ID. - Initiator: The user or account that performed the change. - Action: The type of change (added, edited, deleted). - Configuration Path: The section of the configuration that was modified (e.g., Firewall Policy, Firewall Address). - Object: Specific firewall object affected (e.g., policy name or address group). - Attributes: Key settings or values that were changed Monitoring firewall configurations changes is essential for detecting unauthorized access, preventing misconfigurations, and ensuring compliance with security policies.

RuleName: FTGT-004 - FortiOS version change on Fortinet Devices
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the Fortigate_CL table to detect firmware version changes on Fortinet devices, specifically through the restore-image system action. It identifies and classifies version changes as either an upgrade or downgrade. Firmware downgrades can be a sign of an attempt to exploit older vulnerabilities or bypass newly introduced security mechanisms. Such actions may be initiated by unauthorized administrators or attackers with access to device management. While upgrades are typically legitimate and informational in nature, downgrades pose a potential risk and should be carefully investigated. Alert records: - Time: When the firmware change was initiated. - Device: The name or external ID of the affected Fortinet device. - Operation: Classification of the event as an "Upgrade" or "Downgrade". - Version Info: Original and new firmware versions involved in the change. - Initiator: The identity associated with the request, if available. - Device Action: The system-level action such as restore-image. Monitoring firmware version changes is critical to ensuring device integrity, preventing rollback attacks, and maintaining a secure network posture. This rule helps surface unexpected or potentially risky firmware activities.

RuleName: FTGT-005 - Configuration Download on Fortinet Devices
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the Fortigate_CL table to identify download activities involving system configuration files on Fortinet devices. Downloads of device configurations are a sensitive operation. While such actions are often part of routine administrative maintenance (e.g., backups or audits), they may also signal unauthorized access attempts or pre-attack reconnaissance. In certain attack scenarios, adversaries exploit vulnerabilities to gain access to device configurations, which may include credentials, network settings, and sensitive security controls. This rule excludes known automated scripts from triggering the alert and focuses on identifying manual or unexpected configuration download attempts. Alert Records: - Time: When the configuration download occurred. - Device: Name and external ID of the Fortinet device involved. - User: Account used to perform the download action. - Log ID: Identifier of the security log entry. - Action and Message: The action performed and related log message content. Monitoring this type of event is essential for identifying both legitimate administrative behavior and potentially unauthorized activities involving access to system configurations. These events can have serious security implications and should be reviewed in context.

RuleName: FTGT-006 - Brute-force and Account Enumeration on Fortinet
Description: The rule evaluates Fortinet firewall logs from the Fortigate_CL table to detect two types of suspicious administrative login behavior targeting Fortinet devices. It identifies: - Brute-force attempts against Fortinet’s administrative interface, based on multiple failed login attempts (with invalid passwords) from the same IP address in a short time frame. - Enumeration attempts where attackers use invalid usernames to identify valid admin accounts. If no successful login follows the brute-force attempts, the activity is considered unsuccessful. However, if a successful login is observed shortly after a series of failures, it is flagged as a potentially successful brute-force attack — a critical indicator of compromise. Alert records: - FirstFailure / LastFailure: Timestamps of the first and last failed login attempt. - FirstSuccess: Timestamp of the successful login (if any). - Device: Name, IP, version, and external ID of the Fortinet device targeted. - User: Targeted username(s) and authentication method. - Source IP: Origin of the login attempts. - Activity Details: Type of login event, result reason, and device action. Monitoring this activity helps identify and block attacker behavior early in the intrusion chain. It aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK framework and supports timely incident response.

RuleName: FTGT-007 - Missing Fortinet Audit Logs from Network Device
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the Fortigate_CL table to identify Fortinet devices that have stopped sending log events to Microsoft Sentinel. It analyzes log delivery continuity across all monitored Fortinet systems and flags those that have not sent any logs in the last 90 minutes (configurable threshold) despite activity in the preceding 12-hour observation window. Such gaps in audit logging may indicate potential issues like network misconfiguration, logging service failure, intentional log suppression, or device compromise. Maintaining consistent log flow is critical to ensuring visibility into network security events and supporting incident investigation and compliance efforts. Alert Records: - Device: Name, vendor, product type, and external ID of the Fortinet device. - Time: Timestamp of the last received log from the device. - Time Since Last Log: Human-readable time duration since the last log. - Log Count: Total logs received in the previous 12 hours. - System: Hostname or IP address from which the log was last received. Monitoring for interruptions in Fortinet audit log ingestion helps quickly detect and respond to blind spots in log coverage, ensuring the reliability of detection mechanisms and forensic capabilities.
Req. modification: at least: stream log 0100040704 (40704) and configure config system global set sys-perf-log-interval 30 end.

RuleName: Fortinet Break Glass Account successful logon
Description: The rule detects a successful logon of Break Glass account in to the FortiNet appliance. Is necessarily make a control if the incident is generated.

RuleName: User ignores MFA messages from FortiAuth
Description: User explicitly ignores SMS codes from Forti MFA. This behavior may indicate that login was not expected and the account's credentials may be compromised.

RuleName: FortiAuthenticator Multiple users deleted
Description: Multiple user has been deleted in short time period. Occurring this event can mean an error in the synchronization or compromise of the environment. The incident is created if 20 (threshold) or more users is deleted.

RuleName: FortiAuthenticator service may be unavailable
Description: This rule is designed to automatically monitor the potential unavailability of the FortiAuthenticator service. It tracks key parameters of this service and subsequently alerts if any outage or unusual error messages occur. This allows you to respond quickly to potential authentication issues and ensure uninterrupted system availability.

RuleName: FortiGate IPS event detected from internal IP address
Description: The rule monitors IPS events. If the event is detected from internal IP address of organization than incident is generated. Investigate the incident thoroughly. If the action was blocked than investigate the network traffic and source of attack. The incident may present a vulnerability on the source, malware, or other compromises.

RuleName: High Number of Failed Admin Logins to Fortinet
Description: The rule detects High Number of Failed Admin Logins to Fortinet. If the threshold (5) of Failed login attempts is reached, incident is generated and the used account, IP address and protocol are recorded.

RuleName: FortiGate rule was created or edited where the attribute contains ALL or ANY
Description: The rule monitors ADD and EDIT rule operations on the Fortigate FW appliance where the attribute contains ALL or ANY. The attributes with value ALL or ANY should be used very rarely as they may constitute a breach of network security perimeter. Verify that this change was an authorized by Owner of service.

RuleName: FortiGate Virus Detected and Blocked
Description: The rule evaluating detected and blocked threats on FortiGate firewall appliance. The potential risk is in the possibility of infected file which could be downloaded or runed. In case of an incident, there should always be a user learning experience. Accessing malicious websites that firewall cannot detect and may therefore comprise the environment.

RuleName: Multiple accounts authentication to Forti VPN failed
Description: Identifies multiple accounts who failed to authenticate to Fortinet VPN in short time period. Failed attempts on multiple accounts can be an indication of a password spray attempt.

RuleName: Multiple logons of account to Forti VPN failed
Description: Identifies accounts who have failed to authenticate multiple times in a row to Fortient VPN. Multiple failed attempts can be an indication of a brute force attempt.

RuleName: User Account added to Fortinet_admins group
Description: If the user account is added as member of Fortinet_admins group in Active Directory, the incident is created. The members of Fortinet_admins group gain full administrator permission to ALL Fortinet devices. If the incident is generated, then group membership should be reviewed immediately.

RuleName: GOWO-001 - Google Workspace Role Assignment
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the GoogleWorkspace table to detect role assignments within the Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) environment. It specifically focuses on events generated by the admin application related to delegated_admin_settings, and tracks role assignment operations. The rule identifies when roles—especially critical ones such as super_admin, user_management_admin, security_admin, or cloud_identity_admin—are assigned to user identities. These roles carry elevated privileges that can be misused for administrative access, user management, or security policy changes. Monitoring such assignments is vital as attackers, insiders, or misconfigured automations may exploit elevated privileges to compromise organizational controls or establish long-term persistence. By detecting these changes, this rule helps enforce least-privilege principles and organizational oversight. Alert Records: - Time: Timestamp of the role assignment event. - Initiator: The email address and profile ID of the user initiating the change. - Target: The user email to whom the role was assigned. - Role Details: Assigned role name, severity level (Critical/Non-Critical), and associated IDs. - Location: IP address and geolocation (country and city) from which the assignment was performed. Tracking privileged role assignments supports visibility into identity governance and enhances organizational resilience against privilege escalation attacks or misconfigurations.

RuleName: GOWO-002 - Google Workspace Role Definition Change Activity
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the GoogleWorkspace table to detect changes to custom role definitions within the Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) environment. It monitors events from the admin application associated with the delegated_admin_settings event type and specifically focuses on role management operations such as creation, deletion, renaming, or privilege adjustments. Such changes often reflect administrative configuration actions but can also indicate potential misuse or abuse of role privileges. Attackers or unauthorized users may create or modify roles to escalate privileges, grant excessive permissions, or bypass organizational policies. Alert Records: - Time: When the role definition change occurred. - Initiator: Email address and profile ID of the user who initiated the change. - Operation: Type of action performed (Created, Edited, Deleted). - Role Details: Name and ID of the role affected. - Privileges: Privileges added or removed as part of the action. - Location: Source IP address and geolocation (country and city) of the activity. Monitoring these role management actions is essential to detect potential abuse of administrative rights and maintain secure configurations across the identity environment.

RuleName: GOWO-003 - Organizational MFA Setting Changed in Google Workspace
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the GoogleWorkspace table to detect changes to the "enforce_strong_authentication" setting within the Google Workspace Admin application. The rule specifically identifies when Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is either enabled or disabled at the organizational level. Modifications to MFA enforcement significantly impact the security posture of the organization. Disabling MFA can expose user accounts to credential-based attacks, while enabling it helps prevent unauthorized access and supports compliance with security best practices. These types of changes should be tightly monitored to detect misconfigurations, insider threats, or adversarial actions aimed at weakening authentication policies. Alert Records: - Time: When the change occurred. - Enforce MFA: Indicates whether MFA was enabled or disabled. - Initiator Information: The email address and Profile Id of the user who performed the change. - Initiator IP: Source IP address of the initiator. - Properties: Structured object showing old and new configuration values. - OrgUnitName: The organizational unit affected by the change. Monitoring organizational-level MFA enforcement is critical to ensure that authentication controls remain active, reducing the risk of unauthorized access and supporting compliance frameworks.

RuleName: GOWO-004 - Multiple Admin Role Removals in Google Workspace
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the GoogleWorkspace table to detect the removal of administrative roles from multiple accounts within the Google Workspace Admin environment. It is designed to identify potentially unauthorized or high-impact actions where multiple users are unassigned from roles in a short timeframe. This rule captures all unassignments performed by the same initiator and highlights whether users were removed from single or multiple roles. While such actions may be part of legitimate access cleanup procedures, they could also indicate misuse of privileges, insider threats, or compromised administrator accounts attempting to weaken organizational defenses. The alert includes key contextual information such as the initiator's identity, IP address, number of affected accounts, role names, and time span during which the action occurred. Alert Records: - Start / End Time: Time range of the removal activity. - AdminsRemoved: Total number of users removed from roles. - Role Details: Map of roles and affected users. - Initiator: Email and profile ID of the user who performed the operation. - Source IP / Location: Origin IP address and resolved geolocation. - Operation Duration: Total time span of the removal operation. Monitoring for bulk role removal is essential to identify coordinated privilege changes and prevent situations where administrative visibility or control is lost.

RuleName: Sensitive Azure Key Vault operations
Description: Identifies when sensitive Azure Key Vault operations are used. This includes: VaultDelete, KeyDelete, SecretDelete, SecretPurge, KeyPurge, SecretBackup, KeyBackup. Any Backup operations should match with expected scheduled backup activity.

RuleName: Azure Key Vault access TimeSeries anomaly
Description: Indentifies a sudden increase in count of Azure Key Vault secret or vault access operations by CallerIPAddress. The query leverages a built-in KQL anomaly detection algorithm to find large deviations from baseline Azure Key Vault access patterns. Any sudden increase in the count of Azure Key Vault accesses can be an indication of adversary dumping credentials via automated methods. If you are seeing any noise, try filtering known source(IP/Account) and user-agent combinations. TimeSeries Reference Blog: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/azure-sentinel/looking-for-unknown-anomalies-what-is-normal-time-series/ba-p/555052

RuleName: Mass secret retrieval from Azure Key Vault
Description: Identifies mass secret retrieval from Azure Key Vault observed by a single user. Mass secret retrival crossing a certain threshold is an indication of credential dump operations or mis-configured applications. You can tweak the EventCountThreshold based on average count seen in your environment and also filter any known sources (IP/Account) and useragent combinations based on historical analysis to further reduce noise

RuleName: AD Access denied on multiple folders in short time period
Description: Creates an incident a user has an excessive amounts of denied access to shared folders in Active Directory. Verifying the legitimacy of the operations is highly recommended.

RuleName: AD account with Don't Expire Password
Description: Identifies whenever a user account has the setting "Password Never Expires" in the user account properties selected.

RuleName: AD Emergency Account Successful Logon
Description: The rule detects a successful login by using a emergency (breakglass) account in Active Directory. Is necessary make a control if the incident is generated.

RuleName: AD folder security settings changed
Description: The rule monitors changes in the security settings of a folder in Windows Server Active Directory. You should verify the legitimacy of this operation and do a folder permissions check.

RuleName: Bulk files deleted from shared folder in AD
Description: The rule monitors the bulk deletion of files from shared folders. You should verify the legitimacy of this operation.

RuleName: Bulk object deleted from Active Directory
Description: The rule monitors the bulk deletion of Users and Computer objects and Organizational Unit in the Active Directory.

RuleName: Member added to T0 privileged group
Description: If the member is added in to any Tier 0 Privileged Group, the incident is created. Groups in Tier 0 are the most privileged groups in the domain as Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins etc. If the incident is generated, then group membership should be reviewed immediately.

RuleName: Member added to T1 privileged group
Description: If the member is added in to any Tier 1 Privileged Group, the incident is created. Groups in Tier 1 are the privileged groups in the domain on as SCCM Admins, SCOM Admins, Lepide Admins, SQL Admins etc. If the incident is generated, then group membership should be reviewed immediately.

RuleName: Member added to T2 privileged group
Description: If the member is added in to any Tier 2 Privileged Group, the incident is created. Groups in Tier 2 are privileged groups in the domain as T2-Admin, T2-Coordinators etc. These groups can manage Active Directory on users & computers level. If the incident is generated, then group membership should be reviewed immediately.

RuleName: New user account is created in wrong OU in AD
Description: The rule detects if new user account is created in wrong OU. Monitor creation and modification performed on Active Directory objects to detect ongoing attacks on Active Directory.

RuleName: Primary group of Object in Active Directory has changed
Description: The rule check for changes of value in the primarygroupid attribute. Modification of primary group can be used to store hidden membership as this attribute is not often analyzed. In Active Directory, group membership is stored on the "members" attribute and on the "primarygroupid" attribute. The default primary group value is: 513 - Domain Users, 515 - Domain Computers, 516 – Domain Controllers, 521 – Domain Controllers (Read-Only). The primarygroupid contains the RID (last digits of a SID) of the group targeted. It can be used to store hidden membership as this attribute is not often analyzed.

RuleName: Suspicious activity detected on GPO
Description: The rule monitors activity on Group Policy Objects. New Incident is created if the new GPO created or if the actual GPO is updated, linked, unlinked or deleted.

RuleName: Suspicious events of accounts in Active Directory
Description: The rule looks for a larger number of suspicious events associated with a user account in Active Directory.

RuleName: The Privileged Account has been added to VPN group
Description: If the privileged account is added as member of AllDialupUsersMFA or AllDialupUsers group, the incident is created. VPN groups allow access to internal network and a privileged account can compromise the domain. If the incident is generated, then group membership should be reviewed immediately. Privileged account should be removed from the group and replaced by a non-privileged account.

RuleName: Use Kerberos encryption with DES algorithm
Description: The rule check for uses of DES encryption algorithm. DES is a very weak algorithm and once assigned to an account, it can be used in Kerberos ticket requests, even though it is easily cracked. If the attacker cracks the Kerberos ticket, they can steal the token and compromise the user account. It is recommended to disable DES as an encryption algorithm in the user configuration dialog or in the "msDSSupportedEncryptionTypes" attribute at LDAP level. It has to be disabled in the property of an account by unchecking the box "Use Kerberos DES encryption for this account". References: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/services-hub/health/remediation-steps-ad/remove-the-highly-insecure-des-encryption-from-user-accounts https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/openspecification/msds-supportedencryptiontypes-episode-1-computer-accounts

RuleName: User Account added to ISA_04LIM internet access group
Description: If the user account is added as member of ISA_04LIM internet access group, the incident is created. The ISA_04LIM group allow access to internet where the only limitation is FW. If the incident is generated, then group membership should be reviewed immediately.

RuleName: User account created and deleted within 10 mins
Description: Identifies when a user account is created and then deleted within 10 minutes. This can be an indication of compromise and an adversary attempting to hide in the noise.

RuleName: User account enabled and disabled within 10 mins
Description: Identifies when a user account is enabled and then disabled within 10 minutes. This can be an indication of compromise and an adversary attempting to hide in the noise.

RuleName: Detect CoreBackUp Deletion Activity from related Security Alerts
Description: The query identifies any efforts by an attacker to delete backup containers, while also searching for any security alerts that may be linked to the same activity, in order to uncover additional information about the attacker's actions.' Though such an activity could be legitimate as part of business operation, some ransomware actors may perform such operation to cause interruption to regular business services.

RuleName: Detecting Impossible travel with mailbox permission tampering & Privilege Escalation attempt
Description: This hunting query will alert on any Impossible travel activity in correlation with mailbox permission tampering followed by account being added to a PIM managed privileged group. Ensure this impossible travel incident with increase of privileges is legitimate in your environment.

RuleName: MDXR-001 - Bulk Outgoing Phishing Activity
Description: This rule aims to identify instances of bulk outgoing phishing activity. It evaluates suspicious patterns based on sender information, email attributes such as unique Network Message ID and subject, considering the following criteria: - The number of recipients exceeds 100 or constitutes 50% of the organization's mailbox count. - The time gap between the first and last email is no more than 5 minutes. - The sending occurred from an unusual location (less than 5 mails sent in last 14 days). - Sending was not performed from an IP address listed on the watchlist 'Known_IPs_and_Subnets'. When these criteria are met, an alert is triggered, capturing details such as sender information, recipient list, email subject and Network Message ID, as well as the IP address and location of the sender. The primary goal of this rule is to provide actionable insights into potential phishing attempts. By detecting such activity promptly, organizations can conduct timely investigations and implement necessary mitigation measures to safeguard their systems and data.

RuleName: MDXR-002 - Phishing Verified URL Accessed
Description: The rule evaluates logs from Microsoft Defender XDR and correlates access to URLs with external data from PhishTank to identify potentially malicious activity. When a user accesses a URL that PhishTank has classified as phishing, the rule triggers an alert. If an alert is generated, the following details are recorded: - Account UPN - IP Address - Workload - URL Monitoring and analyzing these alerts are crucial for cybersecurity as they help to identify and mitigate phishing attempts promptly. By tracking such activity, we can prevent credential theft, data breaches, and other potential security incidents that arise from phishing attacks. This proactive approach ensures the protection of sensitive information and maintains the integrity of our network.

RuleName: MDXR-003 - Post-Delivery Email Quarantine Link Click
Description: The rule detects post-delivery email events from Exchange Online (ExO) where an email message is moved to quarantine after being delivered to the inbox folder, and the URL link in the email message was opened by the recipient. The rule correlates events from Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (MDO) and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE). The detection of such events could signify various malicious activities, including phishing attempts, malware distribution, or the presence of misconfigured email filters. These occurrences pose significant security threats to an organization's infrastructure and sensitive data. Left undetected, they could lead to severe consequences such as data breaches, theft of credentials, or the propagation of further malicious activities. If an alert is generated, the following details are recorded: - Post Delivery Time, Delivery Time, Time In Inbox, UrlClickTime - Reclassified Threat - Email Subject and Network Message ID - Recipient, Job Title, Department, Manager - Sender, Sender Domain, Sender IP Address - URL and Attachment Count This comprehensive record ensures that security personnel have access to all pertinent information required to investigate and mitigate potential threats effectively.

RuleName: MDXR-004 - Possible Data Exfiltration to External Disk
Description: The rule detects user-initiated data copying to external devices. It searches for instances where a user creates more than the specified number of files (Threshold) on an external device during a given period. In this manner, it assists in identifying potentially questionable actions associated with transferring data to external drives, which could indicate a potential data exfiltration.

RuleName: MDXR-005 - Potential Build Process Compromise
Description: The query looks for source code files being modified immediately after a build process is started. The purpose of this is to look for malicious code injection during the build process. This query uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint telemetry. More details: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/azure-sentinel/monitoring-the-software-supply-chain-with-azure-sentinel/ba-p/2176463

RuleName: MDXR-006 - Scheduled Task Modification Monitoring
Description: The rule evaluates audit logs from Windows operating systems collected from Security events or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) and detects the creation and modification of scheduled task events. Scheduled tasks are frequently leveraged by malware to establish persistence on a system or execute unauthorized scripts and executables. This rule specifically monitors tasks that involve executable file types or scripting extensions (.cmd, .ps1, .bat, etc.) and flags actions that may indicate suspicious activity, especially when tasks are created with sensitive actions, contain a password, or are located in non-standard paths. To minimize false positives, known safe paths and actions are excluded from detection. Key detection steps: - Collect scheduled task creation and update events from Device Events and Security Event logs. - Identify potentially risky file types and executables within task actions, while filtering out specified known safe actions and paths. Alert records: - Time of event - Task name and action details (e.g., involved scripts or executables) - Device information (e.g., device name, IP address, OS type) - Initiator account details (e.g., account name, domain) This rule enables security teams to efficiently detect and investigate scheduled task modifications that may indicate attempts at persistence or the execution of unauthorized actions, enhancing defenses against potential malware persistence or automated malicious activity.

RuleName: MDXR-007 - Windows Defender Antivirus Disabling Activity Monitoring
Description: This rule detects modifications to critical Microsoft Defender Antivirus registry keys, which indicate that essential features such as Antivirus or Real-Time Protection have been disabled. These changes can significantly weaken endpoint security and should be monitored closely. The rule leverages MDE DeviceRegistryEvents and Windows Security Events to monitor registry modifications to specific DefenderAntivirus-related keys and values (DisableRealtimeMonitoring, DisableAntiVirus, and DisableAntiSpyware), focusing on cases where their value is set to 1. Alert records: - Registry Keys: List of modified registry keys and their associated values. - Initiator: Account and process responsible for the change. - Activity Log: Timeline of registry modification events. - Device Information: Device name, OS platform, type, and IP address. This rule ensures visibility into all scenarios where Microsoft Defender Antivirus features are disabled. By monitoring registry changes, unauthorized tampering can be promptly investigated, helping to identify malware or threat actors attempting to compromise endpoint security. Additional configuration requirements: In addition to enabling the advanced audit "Audit Registry" with "Success and Failure" under Audit Policies, it is necessary to add Audit permissions under the following registry path: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\.
Req. modification: req MDE or SecurityEvents + Auditing of registry for SecEvents.

RuleName: MDXR-008 - PowerShell Command Line - Download and Execute Content
Description: This rule evaluates DeviceProcessEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) and Windows Security Event logs (Event ID 4688) to detect PowerShell commands containing specific keywords that are commonly used to download and execute content from the internet. Downloading and executing potentially malicious content using PowerShell is a critical security concern. This behavior is commonly associated with adversary tactics like file download and execution, which could lead to malware infections or further exploitation of the system. Monitoring this activity aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK techniques T1059.001 - PowerShell. Alert Records: - Time: When the PowerShell command was executed. - Device: The endpoint's name, type (server or workstation), OS, and IP address. - Initiator: The user or process that executed the command, including domain, username, and security identifier (SID). - Command: The PowerShell command executed, along with the detected malicious keywords such as Invoke-WebRequest, IEX, Start-BitsTransfer, etc. By proactively detecting suspicious PowerShell activity, this rule helps organizations mitigate risks associated with the execution of malicious content and improve overall security posture.

RuleName: MDXR-009 - ClickFix Social Engineering Attack Activity on Windows Endpoints
Description: This rule evaluates DeviceProcessEvents from Windows endpoints to identify activities associated with ClickFix social engineering attacks. These attacks often leverage obfuscated or hidden PowerShell execution and connections to remote infrastructure for payload delivery. Threat actors are increasingly using ClickFix techniques to deploy malware, including AsyncRAT, Danabot, DarkGate, Lumma Stealer, and NetSupport, targeting widely used software such as Microsoft Word and Google Chrome. This rule is designed to detect behavioral indicators of compromise associated with ClickFix campaigns, particularly interactive PowerShell execution initiated via explorer.exe. The rule monitors for: * Interactive PowerShell execution initiated by explorer.exe. * Suspicious PowerShell arguments (e.g., hidden window, execution policy bypass, encoded commands). * Obfuscation patterns in PowerShell command lines. * PowerShell activity involving remote URLs or known hosting platforms commonly abused for payload delivery. * Command lines indicative of remote content download. Alert Records: * Time: Timestamp of the detected activity. * Device: Name, type (server or workstation), OS, and IP address of the affected endpoint. * Initiator: The user or process responsible for the activity, including their domain, username, and security identifier (SID). * Description: Behavioral classification of the detected PowerShell activity. * Score: Number of suspicious indicators identified in the command line. Monitoring these activities aligns with security best practices to detect and mitigate risks associated with malware delivery, social engineering abuse, and potential lateral movement.

RuleName: MDXR-010 - Sysinternals Tools Executed with DLL Load from Network
Description: The rule evaluates DeviceEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) to identify instances where Sysinternals tools are executed from network locations and subsequently load DLL files. Such behavior may indicate an attempt to exploit known vulnerabilities within these tools. Attackers can leverage Sysinternals tools executed from network shares to perform unauthorized actions, including privilege escalation or system compromise. By placing malicious DLLs in the same network directory as the Sysinternals executable, attackers can achieve code execution when the tool is run. Alert Records: - Time: When the Sysinternals tool execution occurred. - Device: The endpoint's name, type (server or workstation), OS, and IP address. - Initiator: The user or process responsible for executing the tool, including their account name and security identifier (SID). - File Details: The name and path of the executed Sysinternals tool and the loaded DLL. Monitoring the execution of Sysinternals tools from network locations is essential for detecting potential exploitation attempts, ensuring system integrity, and maintaining secure configurations across the organization’s systems. Ref: https://www.foto-video-it.de/2025/allgemein/disclosure-sysinternals/

RuleName: MDXR-011 - Suspicious FileFix Pattern via Browser on Windows Endpoints
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the DeviceProcessEvents table to detect suspicious command-line activity triggered by internet browsers on Windows endpoints. It focuses on identifying execution patterns consistent with the FileFix technique, a social engineering method where malicious files are designed to launch trusted Windows utilities via browser interaction. The detection targets cases where browsers such as Chrome, Edge, or Firefox initiate execution of potentially dangerous system tools like PowerShell, regsvr32, certutil, or bitsadmin. These tools can be abused to download and execute malicious content, establish persistence, or conduct reconnaissance without requiring explicit user interaction. Alert Records: - Time: When the suspicious process was launched. - Device: Endpoint name, type (server or workstation), OS, and IP address. - Initiator: User or process that launched the browser, including domain, username, and SID. - Process Info: Name of the browser and the system utility that was executed. By correlating the browser as the parent process of suspicious command-line tools, this rule provides visibility into a stealthy and increasingly common execution method exploited by attackers. Reference: https://mrd0x.com/filefix-clickfix-alternative

RuleName: MDXR-012 - Device Code Authentication Phishing Detection
Description: The rule detects key phases of a phishing attack leveraging the Device Code Authentication flow, a method intended for input constrained devices such as smart TVs, printers, or IoT endpoints. Although legitimate, this flow is increasingly abused by attackers to bypass traditional MFA and steal tokens for persistent access. Device Code Phishing campaigns typically follow this pattern: - An email containing a Microsoft device authentication URL is sent to the target (https://microsoft.com/devicelogin or https://login.microsoftonline.com/.../deviceauth) - The victim clicks the link and unknowingly authorizes the attacker's device - The attacker polls Azure AD using the device_code and receives access and refresh tokens after successful user sign-in This rule detects these three stages via distinct alert types: - Device Code Auth URL in Email – a phishing email containing the device auth URL was delivered - Device Code Auth URL Clicked from Email – the user clicked the malicious URL - Successful Sign-in via Device Code Authentication – sign-in completed via deviceCode protocol Each alert can be raised independently, but together they may indicate a high-confidence, multi-step compromise. If all three are observed in sequence, immediate investigation is strongly recommended. The attacker may retain access even if the user resets their password, due to possession of a valid refresh_token. This attack chain is difficult to detect through traditional means, as all user interactions occur via legitimate Microsoft infrastructure.

RuleName: MDXR-013 - Potential Phishing and Malware Delivery via SVG and ZIP Files
Description: This rule evaluates DeviceFileEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) and email telemetry from EmailEvents and EmailAttachmentInfo to detect a suspicious activity chain involving SVG and ZIP files on Windows endpoints. The rule identifies cases where a user saves an SVG file from Outlook and, within 15 minutes, a ZIP file is created by a web browser on the same device and under the same user identity. To improve context, the rule enriches the detection with details from the associated email message, including sender, recipient, subject, and message ID. Attackers may exploit malicious SVG attachments in phishing campaigns, using them to redirect users to credential-harvesting portals or to initiate downloads of password-protected ZIP files carrying malware. By correlating email and endpoint activity, this rule highlights phishing attempts that progress into malware delivery. Alert records: - Times: Creation timestamps of the SVG and ZIP files, including the time difference. - Files & Processes: Names, paths, initiating processes, and hashes of the SVG and ZIP files. - User & Device: UserPrincipalName, DeviceName, and DeviceId. - Email context: Sender address, recipient address, subject, and NetworkMessageId. Monitoring this activity is critical because it connects suspicious email attachments with subsequent endpoint behavior, helping to detect phishing campaigns that attempt to deliver malware.

RuleName: MDXR-014 - Possible Email Spoofing
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the EmailEvents table in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to identify possible spoofed emails. It focuses on inbound messages where the sender's display domain (SenderFromDomain) differs from the envelope domain (SenderMailFromDomain), and where composite authentication mechanisms (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) fail. To reduce false positives, the rule filters out internal email communications, trusted contacts, user-level overrides, and sender domains that have recently sent legitimate emails. It further excludes known bounce messages and empty reverse-path messages. The logic identifies potentially spoofed emails by combining mismatched domain headers with failed authentication, ensuring the sender’s identity cannot be validated. These conditions strongly indicate an attempt to bypass security mechanisms and impersonate a trusted identity. Alert records: -Time: When the suspicious email was received. - Sender: Original email address and spoofed domain used. - Recipient: Email address of the intended recipient. - Mail Server IP: Source IP of the mail server. - Authentication Details: Composite results for SPF, DKIM, DMARC. - Subject: Subject line of the email. - Attachments and URLs: Summary of any files or links in the email. Monitoring this activity is critical for detecting phishing and brand impersonation attempts and for protecting users from fraudulent or malicious messages.

RuleName: MDXR-015 - Shuyal Stealer Malware Activity
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from the DeviceFileEvents and DeviceNetworkEvents tables to identify suspicious activity patterns associated with the Shuyal Stealer malware on Windows endpoints. The rule correlates three distinct behaviors observed on the same host: - Persistence: Creation of an executable file (e.g., host.exe) in the Startup folder, which may allow the malware to execute automatically upon user logon. - Data Staging: Creation of ZIP archive files (e.g., runtime.zip) in the temporary directory, commonly used to package stolen data before exfiltration. - Exfiltration: Outbound communication to the Telegram API domain (api.telegram.org), a known method used by Shuyal Stealer to exfiltrate credentials, browser data, and tokens. When these three indicators are detected together on a single host, it strongly suggests an active compromise involving Shuyal Stealer or similar infostealer malware. Alert records: - Device: The name and hostname of the affected system. - Startup File: The name, path, and timestamp of the file created in the Startup folder, including the initiating process. - Compressed File: The name, path, and creation time of the ZIP file in the temporary folder, including the initiating process. - Network Activity: The Telegram URL or IP contacted, timestamp, and the initiating process that established the connection. Monitoring this combination of persistence, data staging, and suspicious exfiltration methods is critical for identifying modern malware infections early. The Shuyal Stealer malware uses stealthy techniques to remain undetected while stealing sensitive data and exfiltrating it via encrypted messaging infrastructure.

RuleName: MDXR-016 - Lateral Pass-the-Hash Activity on Workstations
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the DeviceLogonEvents table to identify successful NTLM-based logons between two Windows workstations. It focuses on scenarios where lateral movement may occur across endpoints using Pass-the-Hash (PtH) techniques. The detection logic filters for successful NTLM logons in workstation-to-workstation contexts, excluding virtual desktop environments. This activity often indicates that an attacker is using stolen credential hashes to authenticate on another system without knowing the actual password, bypassing normal security controls. Alert records: Time: When the NTLM logon occurred. - Source: The originating workstation’s name and operating system. - Target: The destination workstation’s name and operating system. - Account: The username involved in the logon. - Logon Type: Describes the type of logon session established (e.g., network, interactive). Monitoring NTLM authentication across workstations helps identify lateral movement attempts, which are frequently part of post-compromise activity. This detection supports early discovery of credential abuse and limits the spread of unauthorized access within the organization.

RuleName: MDXR-017 - LDAP Reconnaissance Activity
Description: The rule evaluates DeviceEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) to identify signs of suspicious Active Directory data collection activity using LDAP queries. The rule focuses on LDAP searches that match patterns commonly used by known reconnaissance tools such as SharpHound, AdFind, PowerView, Metasploit, and others. Attackers may use these tools to enumerate users, computers, group memberships, or account attributes in preparation for lateral movement or privilege escalation. The detection relies on a watchlist of known LDAP search filters and excludes system processes or known benign applications to reduce false positives. Alert records: - Time: When the LDAP query was executed. - Device: The endpoint’s hostname and Device ID where the activity was observed. - Initiator: The process name, command line, folder path, and the user context (domain, username, UPN, SID). - LDAP Filter & Tool: The suspicious LDAP filter used and the associated reconnaissance tool inferred (e.g., SharpHound, ADRecon). Detecting unauthorized directory enumeration is crucial for early warning of compromise. Reconnaissance is typically an initial step in targeted attacks and must be addressed proactively to limit the adversary’s knowledge of the environment.

RuleName: MDXR-018 - Mustang Panda PlugX Delivery via HTML Smuggling
Description: This rule evaluates audit events from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) across multiple data sources to detect a specific attack chain associated with the Mustang Panda threat actor using PlugX malware. The detection correlates multiple behaviors commonly linked with this technique: An MSI file written to disk by a browser process, indicating possible HTML smuggling. Execution of known sideloading executables (e.g., gup.exe, robotaskbaricon.exe) via msiexec.exe. Loading of malicious DLLs (libcurl.dll, RoboForm.dll) from the same directory as the sideloading executable. Creation of persistence via registry Run keys from the same process. Attackers like Mustang Panda leverage HTML smuggling to deliver MSI installers that execute sideloading binaries and load malicious DLLs. They often establish persistence by modifying registry keys. This complex behavior chain combines techniques for Initial Access, Execution, Persistence, and Defense Evasion. Alert Records: - Time: Timestamp of the DLL load (execution phase). - Device: Name and ID of the endpoint where the chain was observed. - Dropping Process: Browser used to drop the MSI file. - MSI File: The suspicious installer involved in the attack. - Sideloaded Executable and DLL: Files used in the side-loading technique. - Persistence Registry Key and Value: The registry key path and value written for persistence. Monitoring this behavior is critical because it represents a sophisticated, multi-stage intrusion technique that can lead to full system compromise.

RuleName: MDXR-019 - Active Vulnerabilities Detection
Description: This rule evaluates vulnerability assessment data from the MDETVM_CL table (streamed via Microsoft Defender for Endpoint TVM API), enriched with DeviceInfo and correlated with SecurityAlert records, to identify active and exploitable critical vulnerabilities in environment. The rule focuses on vulnerabilities that meet the following criteria (configurable): - Severity level is Critical. - The vulnerability has a known exploitability level (not marked as NoExploit). - A security update is available. Attackers actively scan for and exploit publicly known critical vulnerabilities, especially when exploit code is available. If security updates are not applied in a timely manner, adversaries may leverage these weaknesses for initial access, privilege escalation, lateral movement, or remote code execution. Alert records: - FirstSeenTimestamp: When the vulnerability was first observed on the device. - LastSeenTimestamp: When the vulnerability was last observed. - DeviceName / DeviceId: The affected endpoint identifier. - Vulnerability: The vulnerable software (vendor and product name). - CveId: Associated CVE identifiers including CVSS score. - Severity: Vulnerability severity level. - ExploitabilityLevel: Exploit availability classification. - OSPlatform / OSVersion: Operating system details of the affected endpoint. Monitoring active and exploitable critical vulnerabilities is essential because these weaknesses represent immediate risk to the organization. Systems with known exploitable CVEs and available patches are prime targets for automated attacks and opportunistic threat actors. Early identification enables prioritization of remediation efforts and reduces exposure to compromise.
Req. modification: watchlist (ReportedMDEvulnerabilities). optionaly PB (SOC_PB_Report_Vulnerability_To_Watchlist). criticality / expoitable. DeviceName regex.

RuleName: ADDS-006 - Active Directory Database Extraction Activity
Description: This rule evaluates Windows Security Events (Event ID 4688) and DeviceProcessEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) to identify suspicious process executions associated with Active Directory database extraction activity. The rule detects command-line patterns and tools commonly used to access, copy, or extract NTDS.dit and related credential material, including NTDSUtil IFM operations, Esentutl access to NTDS paths, direct NTDS.dit file copy or archival activity, shadow copy based NTDS access, registry hive export on Domain Controllers, DiskShadow activity with NTDS context, and Impacket or secretsdump execution patterns. Alert records: - Time when the suspicious process execution was observed. - Host where the activity occurred. - Whether the host is identified as a known Domain Controller. - Account associated with the suspicious process execution. - Process name or process path related to the detected activity. - Classified Active Directory database extraction technique identified by the rule. - Source telemetry table where the activity was observed. Attackers may attempt to extract NTDS.dit and related registry hives to obtain Active Directory credential material, including password hashes and other sensitive authentication data. Successful extraction may enable offline credential extraction, password cracking, privilege escalation, lateral movement, persistence, or full domain compromise.

RuleName: ADDS-010 - Local User Account Created on Windows Endpoint
Description: This rule evaluates DeviceEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) and Windows Security Event logs (Event ID 4720) to detect the creation of local user accounts on Windows endpoints (both servers and workstations). Attackers or malicious insiders may exploit legitimate administrative tools or escalate privileges to create unauthorized local accounts. Such accounts can be used for persistence, bypassing detection, or further system compromise. Monitoring this activity aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1136 - Create Account and is critical for identifying security threats and reducing risks. Alert Records: - Time: When the account creation occurred. - Device: The endpoint's name, type (server or workstation), OS, and IP address. - Initiator: The user or process responsible for creating the account, including their domain, username, and security identifier (SID). - Target: Details of the newly created account, including its username and SID. Monitoring local account creation is critical for detecting potential threats, ensuring accountability, and maintaining secure configurations across the organization’s systems.

RuleName: ADDS-011 - Member Added to Local Group on Windows Endpoint
Description: The rule evaluates DeviceEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) and Windows Security Event logs to detect when a user account is added to a local group on Windows endpoints (both servers and workstations). Adding accounts to local groups is a critical operation that can indicate misconfigurations or malicious activity. Monitoring this behavior aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1136 - Create Account and T1078 - Valid Accounts, focusing on detecting unauthorized changes in group memberships that could lead to privilege escalation or unauthorized access. - Local groups manage access control on individual devices, and unauthorized changes can lead to policy violations or security breaches. - Adversaries may use such changes to gain elevated privileges, bypass authentication mechanisms, or establish persistence. - Tracking these events improves security monitoring and ensures adherence to organizational access control policies. Alert Records: - Time: When the account addition occurred. - Device: The endpoint's name, type (server or workstation), OS, and IP address. - Initiator: The user or process that performed the action, including their domain, username, and security identifier (SID). - Target: Details of the group and the account added to it, including group name, group SID, target username, and SID. By proactively detecting changes in local group memberships, this rule helps organizations mitigate risks associated with unauthorized privilege escalation and enhance their overall security posture.
Req. modification: req Event ID 4798 - A user's local group membership was enumerated to work OK and DeviceEvents (MDE).

RuleName: ADDS-047 - Pass The Hash Activity via NTLM Authentication
Description: The rule evaluates SecurityEvent logs (Event ID 4624) and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) DeviceLogonEvents to identify potential Pass-the-Hash (PtH) activity. It correlates interactive or RDP logons on a source device with subsequent NTLM network logons (LogonType 3) from the same device within a defined correlation window (default 8h). Suspicious behavior is identified when a user (User A) successfully logs on interactively/RDP to a device (SourceHost) and, within the correlation window, the same device initiates an NTLM network logon to a different device (TargetHost) under a different account (User B). This mismatch between the locally authenticated user and the account used for network authentication strongly suggests the use of stolen password hashes. Such behavior may indicate that an attacker has obtained password hashes from a compromised host and is reusing them to authenticate against other systems, enabling lateral movement without needing the plaintext password. Alert records: - Time: When the NTLM authentication occurred. - Source Host: The device from which the NTLM logon originated. - Source IP: IP address of the source host. - Authenticated Account: Account used for the interactive/RDP logon on the source device. - Target Host: The device receiving the NTLM logon. - Target Account: The account being authenticated against on the target device. - Logon Types: Details of both the interactive/RDP logon and the NTLM network logon observed. Monitoring this activity aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1550.002 – Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash and is critical for detecting lateral movement and compromised account usage in Windows environments.

RuleName: ADDS-050 - LSASS Credential Dumping Activity on Windows Endpoint
