Description: TThis rule evaluates Windows Security Events (Event ID 4688) and DeviceProcessEvents from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) to identify suspicious process executions associated with LSASS credential dumping activity on Windows endpoints. The rule detects known tools and command-line patterns commonly used to access or dump LSASS memory, including Mimikatz, SafetyKatz, ProcDump, NanoDump, PPLDump, LSASSY, PyPyKatz, PowerSploit Out-Minidump, Task Manager dump activity, and rundll32 execution of comsvcs.dll MiniDump functionality. Alert records: - Time when the suspicious process execution was observed. - Windows endpoint where the activity occurred. - Account associated with the suspicious process execution. - Process name, process path, and command line related to the detected activity. - Classified LSASS dumping technique or tool identified by the rule. - Process hash, where available. Attackers may attempt to dump LSASS memory to extract credentials, password hashes, Kerberos tickets, or other authentication material that could be used for privilege escalation, lateral movement, or further compromise.

RuleName: CloudApps - Sensitivity Label Downgraded or Removed from file
Description: The rule detects user activity of Sensitivity Label.

RuleName: CloudApp - New Sensitivity Label or Label Policy created
Description: The rule detects the creation of a new Sensitivity label or label policy in Microsoft Purview Information Protection. Verify that this is a legitimate operation. The label can affect the organization's data handling.

RuleName: Logon of several accounts to MS VPN failed
Description: Identifies if several accounts failed authenticate to Microsoft VPN in short time period. Failed attempts on several accounts can be an indication of a password spray attempt.

RuleName: Multiple logons of account to MS VPN failed
Description: Identifies accounts who have failed to authenticate multiple times in a row to Microsoft VPN. Multiple failed attempts can be an indication of a brute force attempt.

RuleName: O365-001 - Accessed files shared by temporary external user
Description: This detection identifies an external user is added to a Team or Teams chat and shares a files which is accessed by many users (>10) and the users is removed within short period of time. This might be an indicator of suspicious activity.

RuleName: O365-002 - Executable file Uploaded to SharePoint or OneDrive
Description: This rule evaluates M365 activities when an executable file is uploaded to SharePoint or OneDrive. The rule searches for specific file extensions ('exe', 'inf', 'gzip', 'cmd', 'bat', 'ps1', 'msi'). The rule also considers where the file was uploaded, with variations being: - Anonymous Share on SharePoint / OneDrive - User OneDrive - Foreign OneDrive - SharePoint The rule records the start and end times of the event, the upload location, user details, the number of uploaded files, the URL location, IP address, and location. This rule enables efficient monitoring and response to potentially risky situations associated with uploading executable files on the M365 platform. This event may be signal a potential risk of creating a space for malware or other malicious activity. We recommend taking immediate steps to investigate and potentially eliminate the threat. Users should be informed of this event and take security measures, including password changes and monitoring for unusual activities.

RuleName: O365-003 - Exchange AuditLog disabled
Description: Identifies when the exchange audit logging has been disabled which may be an adversary attempt to evade detection or avoid other defenses.

RuleName: O365-004 - External user added and removed in short timeframe
Description: This detection flags the occurances of external user accounts that are added to a Team and then removed within one hour.

RuleName: O365-005 - External user from a new organisation added to Teams
Description: The rule identifies external users added to Teams where the user's domain is not one previously seen in Teams data.

RuleName: O365-006 - Multiple Objects Deleted from SPO
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the OfficeActivity table in Microsoft 365 to identify potentially unauthorized deletion of multiple files, folders, or sites in SharePoint Online (SPO). The rule triggers when one of the following thresholds is met within a 2-hour period: - 100 or more files are deleted or recycled. - 20 or more folders are deleted or recycled. - Any single site is deleted or recycled. Alerts are also differentiated based on the operation type: - User moved objects to the Recycle Bin (typically retained for 93 days). - User deleted objects from the First Stage Recycle Bin. - Administrator permanently deleted objects from the Recycle Bin. - User permanently deleted objects (bypassing the Recycle Bin). These behaviors may indicate attempts to intentionally destroy data, disrupt operations, or cover malicious activities. They may also result from unintended user actions, both of which can lead to significant data loss. Alert Records: - Time: When the deletion activity started and ended. - Object Type: File, Folder, or Site. - Count: Number of deleted items. - Operation: The action performed, including the type and severity. - User: The user account performing the operation. - IP Address: Source IP address and geolocation. - Device: Managed or unmanaged status. - Samples: Examples of deleted object identifiers. Monitoring mass deletions in SharePoint Online is essential to ensure data integrity, detect potential malicious actions, and support data recovery efforts when needed.

RuleName: O365-007 - Multiple User Mailboxes Forwarding to Same Destination
Description: The rule evaluates Exchange Online audit logs to identify instances where multiple (current threshold set to 2) users' mailboxes are configured to forward emails to the same destination. The alert records: - IP address and Location - Destination mail address - Number of affected Accounts - Affected Accounts with extended information This detection rule is designed to identify potential security threats where an attacker might have compromised multiple user accounts and configured their mailboxes to forward emails to an attacker-controlled destination. Such activities could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive email communications, resulting in the loss of confidential information and the compromise of multiple user accounts.

RuleName: O365-008 - Multiple files downloaded from SPO or OneDrive
Description: The rule evaluates files download activities from SharePoint Online (SPO) and OneDrive. It considers several factors, including the number of downloaded files (threshold set at 100 files for SPO and 300 files for OneDrive), the type of device, whether it is a managed device, and if the download is from an anonymous link. The alert records: - User ID, IP Address, and Agent - Information about the used device - Sites - Samples of downloaded files This significant file download activity raises concerns about potential data exfiltration or unauthorized access. The large volume of downloaded files, combined with the involvement of a managed/unmanaged device or anonymous share, suggests a deliberate and potentially high-risk action. Immediate investigation is recommended to assess the nature and intent behind this operation, as it may pose a threat to the security of the Microsoft 365 environment. Additionally, monitoring for any abnormal data transfer patterns or further suspicious activities is advised to prevent potential data breaches.

RuleName: O365-009 - Not allowed App added to MS Teams
Description: The rule monitors the status of applications in Microsoft Teams and provides information about their addition. The rule evaluates whether a new app has been added to MS Teams, which hasn't been used in the last 14 days, and also compares the status with the watchlist of 'Teams_Allowed_Applications' of apps in the organization environment. The incident records the identity of the caller, the name of the app, and whether it is allowed or app has been used in last 14 days.

RuleName: O365-010 - Office Policy Tampering
Description: Identifies if any tampering is done to either auditlog, ATP Safelink, SafeAttachment, AntiPhish or Dlp policy. An adversary may use this technique to evade detection or avoid other policy based defenses. References: https://docs.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchange/advanced-threat-protection/remove-antiphishrule?view=exchange-ps.

RuleName: O365-011 - Risky Exchange Online Administrative Operation
Description: This rule evaluates Exchange Online administrative audit events from the OfficeActivity table and correlates them with Microsoft Entra ID sign-in context from SigninLogs. The rule detects selected Exchange Online administrative operations that may affect mail flow, recipient impersonation, mailbox configuration, or Exchange administrative permissions. The monitored operations include recipient permission grants, Exchange Online management role assignments, transport rule creation or modification, and selected mailbox configuration changes. Monitored operations: - Add-RecipientPermission - New-ManagementRoleAssignment - New-TransportRule - Set-TransportRule - Set-Mailbox Alert records include: - Time of the Exchange Online administrative operation. - Initiating account that performed the operation. - Operation name and normalized target object. - Recipient permission details, including granted identity and access rights. - Exchange Online management role assignment details, including role, assignee type, assignee, and scope. - Transport rule or mailbox parameters changed by the operation. - Related sign-in context for the initiating account, including IP address, device information, and location where available. - Detection reason explaining the observed administrative change. These operations may be legitimate administrative activity, but they can also be abused to impersonate recipients, modify mail flow, assign Exchange administrative permissions, configure mailbox forwarding, or alter mailbox behavior. The rule provides operational visibility and prioritizes management role assignments as high severity and recipient permission grants as medium severity.

RuleName: O365-012 - Ransomware Activity Detection on SPO and OneDrive
Description: The rule evaluates audit events in Microsoft 365 (formally Office 365) and looks for activities matching a Ransomware attack on SharePoint Online (SPO) and OneDrive. It examines the quantity of deleted files and recently uploaded (thresholds) files with unfamiliar file extensions, or recognized ransomware file extensions. If such an event is detected, an alert is triggered. The alert records: - User - Caller IP Address - File extension - Current file count - Samples of files - Site URLs Monitoring potential ransomware activity on SharePoint Online (SPO) and OneDrive is crucial for several reasons. SPO and OneDrive often store sensitive and valuable data. Ransomware can encrypt this data, rendering it inaccessible. Early detection through monitoring can help ensure business continuity. Monitoring can help detect ransomware activity early, potentially preventing data loss.

RuleName: O365-013 - SharePoint Anonymous Share Link Created
Description: This rule evaluates Microsoft 365 audit events from the OfficeActivity table to identify the creation of anonymous sharing links in SharePoint Online or related Microsoft 365 workloads. The rule detects SharePoint sharing operations where an anonymous link was created. Anonymous links, also known as Anyone links, allow access to shared content without requiring user authentication and may increase the risk of unintended data exposure. Alert records: - Time when the anonymous sharing link was created. - Microsoft 365 workload where the operation occurred. - User who created the anonymous link. - Managed or unmanaged device indicator. - Source IP address and geolocation details. - SharePoint site URL and relative source path. - Sharing properties such as expiration date, anonymous access flag, share type, granted permissions, and password protection status. This activity may indicate risky external sharing behavior, misconfiguration, or unauthorized sharing performed after account compromise. The rule does not confirm data exfiltration by itself, but identifies creation of an anonymous access path that may enable unverified access to organizational content.

RuleName: O365-014 - SharePoint Sharing Policy Modification at Tenant Level
Description: The rule evaluates OfficeActivity logs and detects changes made to the SharePoint Online (SPO) Sharing Policy at the Tenant level. SharePoint Online allows organizations to control how content is shared both internally and externally. Modifications to these policies, especially at the Tenant level, can have significant security implications. This rule aims to alert security teams when such changes occur, allowing for timely investigation and response. If the Sharing policy is changed, then an alert is generated and records the following: - Caller - Caller IP - Location - Managed device status - Modified Properties of Policy - Tenant ID Overall, this rule enhances the security posture of organizations utilizing SharePoint Online by proactively detecting and responding to unauthorized or unexpected changes in Sharing Policy settings at the Tenant level.

RuleName: O365-015 - Suspicious ExO Inbox Rule Activity
Description: This rule evaluates Exchange Online audit events from the OfficeActivity table to identify suspicious creation or modification of inbox rules. The rule monitors New-InboxRule and Set-InboxRule operations containing actions commonly used after an account compromise to conceal malicious email activity, including deleting messages, forwarding messages, moving messages to another mailbox folder, or marking messages as read. MarkAsRead-only activity is included only when the configured value is True. To reduce false positives, the rule excludes activity originating from exact IP addresses or IPv4/IPv6 CIDR subnets maintained in the Known_IPs_and_Subnets watchlist. Attackers may create or modify inbox rules after compromising a user identity to hide replies, security notifications, delivery failures, or other messages that could reveal fraudulent email activity performed on behalf of the victim. Alert records include: - Time when the inbox rule was created or modified. - Exchange Online organization where the activity was recorded. - Account that performed the operation. - Source IP address, known IP/subnet classification, and associated geographic location. - Operation type and inbox rule name. - Identified suspicious rule actions. - Forwarding recipient, deletion setting, read status, and destination folder, when available. - External access context and the affected Office object. - Complete raw rule parameters for additional investigation. This activity does not by itself confirm account compromise. The detected inbox rule should be reviewed together with previous identity, sign-in, mailbox, and email activity to determine whether the change was authorized.

RuleName: O365-016 - User assigned as Owner of multiple Teams
Description: The rule monitors changes in assigning the Owner role permissions within a Team in Microsoft Teams. This change has the potential to significantly impact the security and integrity of data in team channels. The rule is designed to identify potentially risky situations, such as unauthorized changes and misuse of permissions by users with the Owner role, which could compromise the security and data management in team channels. Alert is generated if: - A member is elevated to the Owner role in at least 5 Teams (Threshold) Alert records: - Member UPN - Teams Names and GUIDs - Iniciator and Inciator ID

RuleName: O365-017 - Potential Forms-based Phishing Email
Description: The rule identifies emails containing links to domains that include "forms." (for example, forms.microsoft.com), where the message also fails one or more authentication checks such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC. Attackers often abuse Microsoft Forms to host phishing pages that mimic legitimate login prompts or surveys in an attempt to collect credentials or personal data. These emails typically bypass standard detection by relying on trusted hosting domains and insufficient sender verification. Alert records: - Time: When the email was received. - Recipient: Targeted mailbox and user object ID. - Subject: Subject line of the email. - URL details: Domain, full link, and detected URL location. - Authentication: Status of SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. - Sender: Display name, sender address, sender IP, geolocation, and domain. - Email metadata: Delivery action, destination folder, and email language. Monitoring this activity is essential because phishing campaigns increasingly use trusted Microsoft infrastructure to deceive recipients. Combining failed authentication with suspicious URLs is a strong indicator of targeted phishing or spoofing attempts.

RuleName: O365-018 - Malware Detection in Microsoft 365 Storage
Description: This rule evaluates OfficeActivity events from Microsoft 365 to identify malware-related operations reported in SharePoint, OneDrive, or other Microsoft 365 storage workloads. The rule detects malware or virus detection operations, including FileMalwareDetected, MalwareDetected, and VirusDetected. It enriches each malware detection event with the last related file action observed on the same Microsoft 365 object within the configured correlation window. Related file actions include file upload, full sync upload, modification, copy, or move operations. Alert records: - Time when the malware-related operation was reported. - Microsoft 365 workload, site URL, object URL, source path, file name, and file extension. - Last related file action, initiator, initiator type, initiator IP address, user agent, managed device status, and client application when available. - Time difference between the last related file action and the malware detection event. - Reporting identity and reporting client application from the malware detection event. - Raw Event_Data and AppAccessContext values for investigation context. This activity may indicate that Microsoft 365 detected malicious or potentially unwanted content in a SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, or related Microsoft 365 storage context. When a previous related file action is available, the initiator represents the account associated with the last observed file action before detection. If no related file action is found, the reporting identity may be a system or application identity and should not automatically be interpreted as the user who uploaded or created the content.

RuleName: O365-019 - Exchange Online Mailbox Permission Granted
Description: This rule evaluates Exchange Online administrative audit events from the OfficeActivity table to identify successful Add-MailboxPermission operations. The rule detects when mailbox permissions are granted to another identity, with a focus on FullAccess permissions. It also identifies self-grant scenarios where the initiating account grants mailbox access to itself. IdentityInfo is used as a best-effort enrichment source to resolve GUID-based identities to user principal names where available. Alert records include: - Time of the Exchange Online permission change. - Initiating account that performed the operation. - Target mailbox or mailbox display name. - Identity that received the mailbox permission. - Granted access right. - Grant classification, including self-granted mailbox permissions. - Detection reason explaining the permission change. Granting FullAccess to a mailbox can allow another identity to open and access mailbox content. Self-granted mailbox permissions are higher risk because they may indicate misuse of administrative privileges, unauthorized access setup, or activity performed from a compromised administrator account.

RuleName: Advanced Multistage Attack Detection
Description: Microsoft Sentinel uses Fusion, a correlation engine based on scalable machine learning algorithms, to automatically detect multistage attacks by identifying combinations of anomalous behaviors and suspicious activities that are observed at various stages of the kill chain. On the basis of these discoveries, Azure Sentinel generates incidents that would otherwise be very difficult to catch.

RuleName: MSSI-003 - Abnormal Increase in Data Ingestion Volume
Description: The rule evaluates audit events from the Usage table to detect abnormal increases in billable data ingestion into Microsoft Sentinel. It compares today's total ingestion volume against the average daily volume calculated over a configurable time window (e.g., 7 days) for each data type. The rule generates an alert if both of the following conditions are met: - The current ingestion volume exceeds the average by more than a defined percentage (current threshold is set to 25%). - The absolute difference in volume surpasses a configured threshold (current threshold is set to 300 MB). These patterns may indicate potential misconfigurations, anomalous spikes in telemetry, or deliberate attempts to flood the SIEM with large volumes of irrelevant data. Such behavior can degrade system performance, obscure genuine alerts, or signal underlying security incidents. Alert Records: - Data Type: The type of ingested data that exhibited the anomaly. - Today’s Volume (MB): The current day’s total ingestion for the data type. - Average Volume (MB): The average daily ingestion volume over the past 7 days. - Difference (MB): The absolute volume change from the average. - Change (%): The percentage difference compared to the average. - Trend: Whether the change is an increase or drop. Monitoring these anomalies helps identify risks related to unexpected ingestion growth, possible security misconfigurations, or overcollection that could strain the SIEM’s capacity and effectiveness.

RuleName: Data connector does not send data to the workspace
Description: This detection will go over the last log received from the listed Connectors. If the last log form connector is older than 3 hours, then incident is created. Please check the connector health. You can use Data collection health monitoring workbook for the additional investigation.

RuleName: MSSI-001 - Log Analytics Daily Cap and Data Retention Monitoring
Description: This rule evaluates log entries from the _LogOperation table in Microsoft Sentinel to monitor changes to the daily data ingestion quota, data retention settings, and quota compliance events. The query identifies: - Adjustments to the daily ingestion cap: Including the new and previous values, along with the identity of the user who initiated the change. - Changes to data retention settings: Capturing updates to the retention period, the new and previous values, and the user responsible. - Quota compliance events: Monitoring when data ingestion is halted or resumed due to reaching or respecting quota limits. Unexpected changes to ingestion quotas, retention settings, or interruptions in data collection may indicate unauthorized actions, misconfigurations, or attempts to evade detection by overwhelming or manipulating log systems. Such tactics can disrupt security monitoring. Monitoring these events helps ensure the reliability and continuity of security systems. Alert Records: - Time: When the quota or retention change or status event occurred. - Details: Previous and new daily ingestion limits, data retention periods, or the status of quota adherence (e.g., ingestion stopped or resumed). - Initiator: The user or process responsible for the change, including username and security context. By monitoring changes to ingestion quotas, retention periods, and quota adherence events, this rule helps organizations detect and mitigate potential attacks targeting security monitoring systems, ensuring the reliability and availability of threat detection mechanisms.

RuleName: MSSI-002 - Microsoft Sentinel Content Modified by Unapproved Caller
Description: The rule evaluates Microsoft Sentinel audit logs (such as AzureActivity, SentinelAudit, and SentinelHealth) to detect unapproved modifications to Sentinel resources and content. Unauthorized changes to Sentinel components may indicate compromised accounts, insider threats, or operational misconfigurations, potentially impacting the platform's ability to detect and respond to security incidents. This monitoring aligns with best practices for securing operational environments and supports compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements. Monitored actions include: - Analytics rules: Creation, updates, deletion, or disabling. - Automation rules: Creation, updates, or deletion. - Playbooks: Creation, updates, deletion, enabling, or disabling. - Incidents: Deletion. - Tables: Creation, updates, or deletion. - API Connections: Creation, updates, or deletion. - Workbooks and Watchlists: Creation, updates, or deletion. Alert records: - Time: Timestamp of the detected modification. - Action: Specific activity performed (e.g., rule update, playbook deletion). - Resource details: Name, type, and ID of the modified resource. - Caller: Identity of the individual or process initiating the modification, including UPN or application ID. - IP Address and location: Origin of the action, including geolocation information. Rationale and implications: - Sentinel resource modifications should only be performed by authorized administrators or applications to prevent misuse or accidental disruptions. - Unapproved changes can suppress alerts, alter configurations, or lead to blind spots in detection mechanisms. - By detecting these activities in real-time, organizations can mitigate risks, ensure accountability, and maintain system integrity. Recommended response: When an incident is generated, security teams should immediately review the alert to verify the caller's legitimacy and investigate the intent behind the modification. Prompt action is necessary to prevent potential security breaches or operational impacts.

RuleName: MSSI-004 - Missing Heartbeat from Windows or Linux Machine
Description: This rule evaluates heartbeat events from the Heartbeat table to identify Windows or Linux machines that have stopped sending heartbeat data to Microsoft Sentinel within the defined time threshold. The rule detects monitored machines reporting through Azure Monitor Agent or Direct Agent whose last heartbeat is older than the configured period. It also identifies whether the affected machine is listed as a Domain Controller and adjusts severity accordingly. Missing heartbeat activity may indicate that the machine is offline, unreachable, improperly configured, or no longer sending telemetry due to agent failure, service disruption, or malicious interference. Alert records: - Time of the last received heartbeat and number of minutes since the last heartbeat - Affected machine - OS informations - Last known public and private IP addresses - Environment and category Monitoring this activity is important because loss of heartbeat may reduce visibility into the affected system and may indicate operational issues or intentional attempts to disable monitoring.

RuleName: Status of incident has been changed
Description: The rule monitors incident status changes. An alert is generated when the owner is assigned, or any other incident status is changed. Alert is the trigger for the Playbook. The Playbook notifies the owner via email. This rule do NOT create a new incident.

Description: The member has been removed to administrative role. Please verify the operation is correct. Unauthorized tampering with the administrator's authorization can result in a hight security incident.
